And even now I need to improve, I need to be better. "It's a lot of hard work." Rooney's move to broadcasting after a stellar playing career - followed by a testing stint as a manager - has not always been smooth. His debut as a full-time pundit on Match of the Day in August 2025 divided opinion, with one fan writing on social media: "Just because you have done something, does not automatically make you good to talk/explain and teach others well." Guardian journalist Paul MacInnes was more upbeat about Rooney's debut. "He's articulate, and on Saturday night was able to conjure up the right word when you could see he was looking for it," he wrote. "He is tactically insightful and has a wealth of experience to draw from too." As a player, Rooney learned from managers including Sir Alex Ferguson and David Moyes, and won the Champions League, Europa League, Premier League (five times), FA Cup and League Cup (three times). He was not always the most articulate in his post-match interviews. As a pundit, he has found his voice. In an attempt to better himself as a broadcaster, Rooney has sought feedback and advice from experienced television executives, as well as other players-turned-pundits including Alan Shearer, Danny Murphy, Hart and Micah Richards. "I do look at the other pundits who have been there a long time," added Rooney. "I see how they do it. I enjoy it, it keeps me involved in football." Asked about dealing with criticism from people watching him on TV, Rooney responded: "You do see it. "It drives me to be better. I always feel when I do something I want to do better and be the best I can." Paul Stretford, Rooney's long-serving agent, said people should not be surprised by what his client can achieve. "It is no surprise to me that Wayne has continued to put his doubters in their place with his football intelligence and straightforward manner," added Stretford. "Time and time again as a player he was able to raise his game to incredible levels. "They should also not be surprised at his drive and ambition to be the best that he can possibly be. And he does this with a combination of intelligence and humility." Philip Bernie, head of BBC Sport events, said Rooney had shown a "great willingness to learn and determination to improve" as a broadcaster. "Wayne is also a very likeable guy, a proper team player, with no ego on display," he added. As well as developing chemistry with his fellow pundits, Rooney has changed his appearance after committing to a healthier lifestyle through a fitness regime which involves games of padel and boxing training. "Like anyone who cares about their job, Wayne had to work hard - to learn skills around analysis and delivery - and he's improved so much in a short time," said Alex Kay-Jelski, director of BBC Sport. "Micah and Joe alongside him at the World Cup were perfect team-mates - three equals - and you'll be seeing more of them together on the BBC in coming seasons." Their chemistry was obvious in the summer, particularly when they swapped their microphones for oars after an erroneous Rooney prediction. He pledged to row down the River Mersey if Norway beat Brazil, and when they did, he confirmed on air he would adapt the challenge to do it in the United States. That led to him, Hart and Richards to take to the Hudson River in New York. "Wayne deserves this so much," added Kay-Jelski. "He's a great mix of incredibly clever, funny in a self-deprecating manner and likeable. "From a BBC side he's easy to work with, treats everyone the same whether they're a former team-mate or starting out in a junior position, and his words carry real weight." item.title: ‘I have been subject to a lot of hate’: RCB star reveals how fans trolled him whenever Shubman Gill hit a ton
item.description: Venkatesh Iyer has opened up about the prolonged online backlash he faced from Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) supporters following the franchise's decision to retain him while releasing Shubman Gill ahead of IPL 2022. The Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) batter revealed that the criticism has continued over the years, with fans still targeting him whenever Gill scores a century. Gill was released by KKR ahead of the 2022 season and subsequently became one of the three players drafted by the newly formed Gujarat Titans (GT), who secured his services for Rs 8 crore alongside Hardik Pandya and Rashid Khan. Speaking in a podcast with Aakash Chopra, Venkatesh recalled how KKR supporters have repeatedly brought up the franchise's decision, making him a target of social media trolling. "I have been subject to a lot of hate for a long time. Even till date, if Shubman is getting a hundred; you go to a KKR page, people would be commenting, 'in search of gold, we lost a diamond' and all of that stuff," Venkatesh said. The 31-year-old also discussed his situation ahead of the IPL 2026 auction, particularly after KKR decided to release him. He revealed that he had even approached franchise co-owner Shah Rukh Khan in the hope of a change in the decision. "I had kept an hankerchief on the side. I even asked Shah Rukh sir," he said. KKR had spent Rs 23.75 crore to buy Venkatesh back ahead of the 2025 season. However, following his release, the all-rounder admitted that he had already moved on mentally and was not even considering a return to the franchise during the 2026 auction. "I didn't even think about the pay cut. I had already started thinking, 'Okay, it's not going to be purple'," he said. Venkatesh was eventually signed by defending champions RCB, where he got an opportunity to experience a completely different fan culture. The batter was particularly struck by the devotion of Bengaluru supporters and described their connection with the franchise as something he had never witnessed before. "You won't believe this, but I saw people actually worshipping the RCB jersey before matches. This was something different. Fandom at a different level," Venkatesh recalled. His initial days at RCB involved spending time on the bench before he was introduced as an Impact Substitute after the team suffered an early collapse in the batting order. He responded with an unbeaten 29 off 15 deliveries, helping RCB reach 201/8, although the team eventually lost the match. Venkatesh later delivered another impressive performance against Punjab Kings, remaining unbeaten on 73 off 40 balls. He ended the season with 209 runs from seven matches at an average of 52.25, playing his part in RCB's successful campaign as the franchise secured its second IPL title in a row. 135591640

"I didn't even think about the pay cut. I had already started thinking, 'Okay, it's not going to be purple'," he said. Venkatesh was eventually signed by defending champions RCB, where he got an opportunity to experience a completely different fan culture. The batter was particularly struck by the devotion of Bengaluru supporters and described their connection with the franchise as something he had never witnessed before. "You won't believe this, but I saw people actually worshipping the RCB jersey before matches. This was something different. Fandom at a different level," Venkatesh recalled. His initial days at RCB involved spending time on the bench before he was introduced as an Impact Substitute after the team suffered an early collapse in the batting order. He responded with an unbeaten 29 off 15 deliveries, helping RCB reach 201/8, although the team eventually lost the match. Venkatesh later delivered another impressive performance against Punjab Kings, remaining unbeaten on 73 off 40 balls. He ended the season with 209 runs from seven matches at an average of 52.25, playing his part in RCB's successful campaign as the franchise secured its second IPL title in a row. 135591640

item.content:encoded: Fernando Forestieri has gone from playing in the top leagues in Italy and Spain to signing for Oxford City [Oxford City] A Saturday afternoon in October at the Hebburn Sports and Social Ground, Tyne & Wear. Some Hebburn Town fans are already heading for the exits as Oxford City, 3-0 up in the 81st minute, send on their new signing. Fernando Forestieri has shared pitches with Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Zlatan Ibrahimovic, and played in front 72,000 fans at Real Madrid's iconic Bernabeu Stadium. On this occasion, down in English football's sixth tier, there are 873 supporters present to witness Oxford City's new Argentine number 15 come on for his debut. "It was like a tennis match, the ball going one way one second, then the other way the next," Forestieri, 36, told BBC Sport after his new club, nicknamed the Hoops, secured a seventh win in 11 games to sit third in National League North. On Friday, Oxford City host Leicester City in the first round of the FA Cup (19:45 GMT), with former Watford and Sheffield Wednesday forward Forestieri looking to inspire the non-league club to a famous win over the League One Foxes. It is 10 years since Leicester famously won the Premier League title. In the same season Forestieri was helping Sheffield Wednesday reach the Championship play-off final, where the Owls lost to Hull City at Wembley. "There's a big gap between what Leicester did 10 years ago and where they are now," he said. "Why can't Oxford City cause an upset? This is what the FA Cup is all about." Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City Forestieri encountered Barcelona, Messi and Ibrahimovic while playing for Malaga in Spain's top flight in 2009-10. Meanwhile, he shared the same pitch with Ronaldo as recently as five years ago when Juventus played Forestieri's Udinese team in Serie A. "You never forget being on the same pitch with these big players," added Forestieri, whose CV includes scoring against Inter Milan for Siena in 2008. "Messi, Ronaldo, Ibrahimovic... unbelievable skills. "I'm very lucky. Being that close to them you remember their first touch, their vision." Forestieri grew up playing football on the streets of Rosario - the same city in Argentina Messi was born - and idolised Diego Maradona. When Maradona died in 2020, Forestieri wrote a tribute to the 1986 Argentina World Cup winner on the back of his Udinese shirt. "Growing up in Argentina, everyone pretended to be Diego," he said. "He was a hero to everyone. On every corner of every street someone painted his face on a wall." Talking about his childhood, Forestieri said: "I was born poor, born with nothing. "I lived with my mum and dad and two brothers. The five of us slept in one room." Rosario was a dangerous area and Forestieri's brother, Maximiliano, was shot and wounded. "Thankfully he survived," said Forestieri, who was part of the academies of famed Argentine clubs Newell's Old Boys and Boca Juniors. Aged 16, he moved to Italy and quickly made his senior debut for Genoa. He qualified to play for Italy through his grandfather and turned out for the Azzurri at youth levels. Twenty years after his senior debut for Genoa, and after recent spells in Malaysia and Cyprus, he is still playing - albeit in non-league, after returning to England following the birth of his third son, Luciano. Forestieri (left) aged 18, in action for Siena against AC Milan's Andrea Pirlo in 2008 [Getty Images] So, how did his move to Oxford City come about? Forestieri was at Watford at the same time as Hoops boss Ross Jenkins, while Oxford City assistant manager Paul Robinson is also a former Hornets player. He trained with the PFA as part of their pre-season programme for players without a club before getting a call from Robinson. "Robbo said: 'why you don't come here to help us? We'll help you to become fit'," explained Forestieri. "For me this is a big change. But I'm so happy to be at Oxford City. They are an ambitious club and I want to help them as much as I can." Forestieri paid tribute to Diego Maradona on the back of his Udinese shirt following the death of the Argentina legend in 2020 [Getty Images] The player, who is also taking his coaching badges, lives in north London with his wife, Andria, and their two other sons Santiago, aged nine, and Maximiliano, aged six. "I still have passion for football," he added. "Whenever I'm walking in the park with Santiago and we see someone playing football, we stop and join in. That's how much I still love football." Since making his debut against Hebburn, Forestieri has appeared in league games against Marine, Merthyr and South Shields. After the money-spinning Leicester tie, which is expected to attract a 3,500 sell-out crowd, Oxford City - who sit second in National League North - return to the north-east to play Darlington in a league match next Tuesday. "You need to listen to your body when you reach 36," said Forestieri. "But I'm lucky to be still playing and that a club still wants me to play for them." item.title: A Scottish influence has transformed New Zealand – but can the Scots finally beat the All Blacks?
item.description: The New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie took plenty from his three years at the Glasgow Warriors but it is the chuckles that he remembers most fondly. “The Scottish are funny people and I haven't laughed as much in any environment as much as I have in my time here,” Rennie explained back in 2020 after embarking on what proved an ill-fated stint with Australia. “I've loved the people and I've loved our time here. It's been special, we'll miss it.” Dave Rennie spent three years at Glasgow (Getty) Perhaps it is no surprise, then, that there has been such a strong Scottish influence at the heart of his project to restore the All Blacks ’ spirit. Mike Blair won 85 caps at scrum half and captained Scotland 14 times; until deciding he rather preferred life overseeing attack, it appeared he was being groomed as Gregor Townsend ’s successor in the highest coaching office in the land. Instead, he and Rennie return to Murrayfield with a New Zealand side in a phase of reinvention or rediscovery – re-finding the tenets that made them great and forging perhaps the world’s most outstanding attack. It has proved a natural fit. Blair has admitted to feeling a degree of impostor syndrome when he first came into All Blacks camp earlier this year, but has found the squad highly receptive to his methods. He has done excellent work, too, getting a tune out of a series of playmakers and associated parts through a demanding itinerary. Unbeaten so far in the Nations Championship having overcome France, Italy and Ireland in July, they carry confidence from two professional performances against the Wallabies last month. “We're in a good place, I think,” Blair said this week. “We’re pleased with what we did against Australia but we're also aware that playing Scotland at Murrayfield is a really big challenge. It's another good opportunity to show the growth in our game.” Scotland struggled to get close to New Zealand during the playing days of Mike Blair (far left) (Getty) The former scrum half made a self-deprecating crack that he’d already contributed to a few All Blacks wins over Scotland this week but his own playing days do serve as a reminder of how this challenge has changed for the tourists. Back when their attack coach wore the thistle, the result was a foregone conclusion; in four meetings with the All Blacks as a player, Blair only got within 20 points once. "When I played, New Zealand played their second-string team. item.content:encoded: The New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie took plenty from his three years at the Glasgow Warriors but it is the chuckles that he remembers most fondly. “The Scottish are funny people and I haven't laughed as much in any environment as much as I have in my time here,” Rennie explained back in 2020 after embarking on what proved an ill-fated stint with Australia. “I've loved the people and I've loved our time here. It's been special, we'll miss it.” Dave Rennie spent three years at Glasgow (Getty) Perhaps it is no surprise, then, that there has been such a strong Scottish influence at the heart of his project to restore the All Blacks ’ spirit. Mike Blair won 85 caps at scrum half and captained Scotland 14 times; until deciding he rather preferred life overseeing attack, it appeared he was being groomed as Gregor Townsend ’s successor in the highest coaching office in the land. Instead, he and Rennie return to Murrayfield with a New Zealand side in a phase of reinvention or rediscovery – re-finding the tenets that made them great and forging perhaps the world’s most outstanding attack. It has proved a natural fit. Blair has admitted to feeling a degree of impostor syndrome when he first came into All Blacks camp earlier this year, but has found the squad highly receptive to his methods. He has done excellent work, too, getting a tune out of a series of playmakers and associated parts through a demanding itinerary. Unbeaten so far in the Nations Championship having overcome France, Italy and Ireland in July, they carry confidence from two professional performances against the Wallabies last month. “We're in a good place, I think,” Blair said this week. “We’re pleased with what we did against Australia but we're also aware that playing Scotland at Murrayfield is a really big challenge. It's another good opportunity to show the growth in our game.” Scotland struggled to get close to New Zealand during the playing days of Mike Blair (far left) (Getty) The former scrum half made a self-deprecating crack that he’d already contributed to a few All Blacks wins over Scotland this week but his own playing days do serve as a reminder of how this challenge has changed for the tourists. Back when their attack coach wore the thistle, the result was a foregone conclusion; in four meetings with the All Blacks as a player, Blair only got within 20 points once. "When I played, New Zealand played their second-string team. They gave guys opportunity against us," he admitted. ”Times have changed from that.” The last four meetings have been decided by eight points or fewer. Scotland will rue missed opportunities in at least two of those, including last year – having hauled the game back to level pegging from 17-0 down, Townsend’s side could not sustain their effort. One could feel echoes of that game during a not dissimilar defeat to South Africa during the first phase of the Nations Championship in July – this tournament may have its critics but in ensuring a regularity of fixture against the very top teams, it is of great benefit to Scotland. Will that translate into the next step of finally beating New Zealand? The fear of some is that last year represented a significant missed opportunity against a team in flux. While consistency and coherence in selection puts Scotland in a good place, they will be at a disadvantage in starting a campaign against an international team that has been together virtually since July. No doubt, though, that Townsend will want his team to try to match their expressive visitors stride-for-stride. Damian McKenzie’s try helped New Zealand beat Scotland in a Murrayfield thriller last year (PA Wire) “It’s obviously an exciting occasion getting to play the All Blacks,” said the lock Scott Cummings. “The build-up probably feels a bit different this time because the last couple of times we’ve played them it’s been three or four years (since the previous meeting) but we got to play them last year, so we know what to expect from them. Obviously they’re a quality outfit and we know we need to be at our best on the day to beat them. I believe we can do that.” Confidence will be taken from the strong start enjoyed in the United Rugby Championship by both Scottish sides, with Edinburgh joining Glasgow among the early pace-setters. Townsend has largely put trust in those who have served him well before, but the form of Liam McConnell, Freddy Douglas and others deepens the pool the options. They may be required in a busy November. Those rigours will be felt, too, by a New Zealand squad entering the final stretch of a gruelling international itinerary that began at the start of July. This has been a tough week, too, after the sudden passing of security chief Logan Cadwallader in Edinburgh . The All Blacks will carry his memory on to the field. “Logan has been a big part of the All Blacks family for a long time,” Rennie said. “He was the ultimate team man, loved and trusted by all and a true professional. He looked after all of us, players and staff, and he was a good mate to many in this team. We are all devastated. As a team, we will honour Logan and the legacy he has left on the All Blacks.”

item.title: The Outlook - Week 9 (CLE-NO, NYG-PHI, LAR-WAS, DEN-CAR, HOU-LAC)
item.description: Hey, folks! We’re back with our second block of games for the Week 9 NFL slate, and we’re staying with the early games here. We have the remaining games that we didn’t cover in the first block, plus a late game featuring HOU-LAC due to the uneven schedule! We’ve compiled the groupings of games here to make it easier to find the games you want: Block 1: JAC-BAL, CIN-ATL, DAL-IND, NYJ-KC, DET-MIA Block 2: CLE-NO, NYG-PHI, LAR-WAS, DEN-CAR, HOU-LAC Block 3: LV-SF, GB-NE, ARI-SEA, TB-CHI, BUF-MIN “The Outlook” will give you the details, stats, analysis, recommendations and everything else you need to make informed fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team will be profiled in this article. We want everyone reading this to bring home championships in their fantasy leagues! I’m incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season, and I hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) or tag me in a post with any lineup questions. I’ll do my best to answer them for you. Let’s get into it! All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Wednesday for CLE-NO, NYG-PHI, LAR-WAS, DEN-CAR and HOU-LAC. Teams on bye in Week 8: Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints Favorite: Saints –3 Game Total: 42.5 Implied Point Total: Saints 22.75, Browns 19.75 Browns Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: None Browns QBs With Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol and potentially missing this week’s game against the Saints in New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start if Watson cannot clear protocol in time. Honestly, it’s probably a slight negative for the offense’s efficiency, but last season, we saw a noticeable uptick in tight end targets with Sanders at quarterback. Either way, regardless of who starts for the Browns, neither quarterback is a safe start outside of superflex or two-quarterback leagues. Fantasy Advice: Count me out on either Watson or Sanders in single-quarterback leagues. As a low-end QB2 in superflex, either one would be a decent start against a Saints defense that will give up some production, particularly to tight ends. RB Quinshon Judkins The Browns threw 41 times and managed just 12 running back carries as they fell behind 20-6 at halftime and then 27-6 in the third quarter. That ended up being the final score in Pittsburgh against the Steelers in Week 8. Judkins led the Browns in carries (11) but could manage only 25 yards on the ground, with another 24 through the air. It was actually Dylan Sampson who led the Browns running backs in routes and snaps, but that was a product of game script more than anything. With the Saints on tap in Week 9 and allowing a whopping 4.9 yards per carry and the most fantasy points to opposing backfields, Judkins can really settle in for some excellent production in this game if the Browns can hang with the Saints. Teams on bye in Week 8: Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints Favorite: Saints –3 Game Total: 42.5 Implied Point Total: Saints 22.75, Browns 19.75 Browns Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: None Browns QBs With Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol and potentially missing this week’s game against the Saints in New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start if Watson cannot clear protocol in time. Honestly, it’s probably a slight negative for the offense’s efficiency, but last season, we saw a noticeable uptick in tight end targets with Sanders at quarterback. Either way, regardless of who starts for the Browns, neither quarterback is a safe start outside of superflex or two-quarterback leagues. Fantasy Advice: Count me out on either Watson or Sanders in single-quarterback leagues. As a low-end QB2 in superflex, either one would be a decent start against a Saints defense that will give up some production, particularly to tight ends. RB Quinshon Judkins The Browns threw 41 times and managed just 12 running back carries as they fell behind 20-6 at halftime and then 27-6 in the third quarter. That ended up being the final score in Pittsburgh against the Steelers in Week 8. Judkins led the Browns in carries (11) but could manage only 25 yards on the ground, with another 24 through the air. It was actually Dylan Sampson who led the Browns running backs in routes and snaps, but that was a product of game script more than anything. With the Saints on tap in Week 9 and allowing a whopping 4.9 yards per carry and the most fantasy points to opposing backfields, Judkins can really settle in for some excellent production in this game if the Browns can hang with the Saints. Fantasy Advice: If I’m a Judkins manager, I’m hoping the Browns can generate some offense and stay in the game against the worst defense against fantasy running backs so far this season. I have Judkins as a high-end RB2 here for Week 9. Browns WRs In a negative game script that lasted from around halftime through the end of the game, some of the Browns’ pass-catchers had a chance to stretch their legs. Some, not all. Denzel Boston falls into the “some” bucket, as he earned 11 targets but couldn’t do too much with a 6-37-0 line. That’s the rub with these Browns wide receivers: You can get volume, but efficient volume is another story and remains a consistent work in progress. We know Boston is typically a deeper-aDOT receiver, so he’s bound to connect on those deeper opportunities on a coin-flip basis. That’s why he’s still worthy of a fantasy start. In the “not all” bucket is KC Concepcion , who caught all three of his targets for 37 yards despite the team attempting 41 passes. That’s just an 8.1% target share, folks. When we talk about volatility, this is a perfect example of a bad team with young receivers who are still very difficult to rely on for fantasy production each week. Both Boston and Concepcion are startable, but it’s definitely caveat emptor with all Browns players, especially these rookie receivers. Fantasy Advice: With the possibility that Sanders could start instead of Watson, the calculus for the Browns’ receivers doesn’t change too much. Still, they’re both nothing more than flex plays against the Saints, with a volatile range of outcomes. TE Harold Fannin Jr. It may have taken seven weeks, but Watson finally remembered that he has a tight end at his disposal who broke records in college and was awesome as a rookie. That’s Fannin, who has put up 16 receptions and 245 yards on 19 targets over the last two weeks. The Saints have allowed the sixth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season. If Sanders ends up starting, he was the quarterback who helped Fannin produce so favorably in the first place last season. It’s a great matchup, and for you Fannin enjoyers out there (also very much me), things couldn’t set up much better, despite the uncertainty surrounding which quarterback will start. Fantasy Advice: Fannin is a great start this week as a mid-range TE1, but I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention that some of the volatility surrounding the Browns’ offense also applies to Fannin. Saints Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: WR Chris Olave QB Tyler Shough After finishing as a top-eight fantasy quarterback in each of the first three weeks of the season, Shough has been very inconsistent over his next four games. His only game with more than 16 fantasy points during that stretch was his Week 6 matchup against the Giants, when he accounted for three passing touchdowns and a rushing score while leading the Saints to a comeback victory after scoring 34 unanswered points on the road. The Saints had their bye in Week 8, so hopefully they’ll get their passing game back on track here against the Browns at home. Unfortunately, the Browns are a severe run funnel and play the pass well, so Shough has a tough matchup ahead of him. Fantasy Advice: Shough is perfectly fine in multi-quarterback leagues as a QB2, but I’d certainly have some reservations about starting him against the Browns in single-quarterback leagues. Saints RBs This backfield is as murky as it gets. If it’s just Kendre Miller and Alvin Kamara , the backfield becomes much easier to parse, with Miller handling most of the low-value touches and Kamara getting the receiving work. I’d rather have Kamara because receiving work is worth more than carries. However, in a good matchup like this against the Browns, both backs could have some utility. We’ll see if CJ Donaldson (shoulder) will be able to play, but Travis Etienne (hamstring) is expected to return to practice soon, and the team also signed Audric Estime . Between now and Sunday, it remains to be seen which combination of backs the Saints will deploy against Cleveland. Fantasy Advice: Even with a great matchup, both Miller and Kamara are still just flex plays without much upside. WR Devaughn Vele All season, Vele has been a solid, no-nonsense flex play, as he’s run routes on 92% of dropbacks. That said, the Saints opened the practice window for Jordyn Tyson , so Vele’s fantasy relevance could be coming to an end once Tyson gets up to speed. However, let’s not cry over what we had; smile because it happened! Tyson may not be ready to go immediately, so Vele should be very playable this week as a low-end flex. Managers should be ready to pivot away from Vele if his production slows to a crawl or his routes decrease, however. More than likely, though, it’s going to be Bryce Lance who feels the squeeze in routes, not Vele. Fantasy Advice: It’s a tougher matchup against the Browns, who have been very good against the pass this season, but Vele’s routes and role in the offense make

item.title: Knicks Star Calls Taylor Swift Their ‘Fakest Fan’ With ‘Performative’ Dig — Source
item.description: Photo Credit: Perry Knotts/Getty Images Sport via Getty Images Taylor Swift has recently been labeled the “fakest celebrity Knicks fan,” as New York Knicks player Tyler Kolek took a dig at the global pop star on “NBA 2K League.” He told his teammate, Deuce McBride, that Swift’s appearance at the games is likely “performative.” While the two agreed that Swifties might criticize them brutally online, Kolek still reportedly disapproved of the singer being a Knicks fan. Knicks star Tyler Kolek brands Taylor Swift their ‘fakest fan’ in new show video View this post on Instagram Knicks star player Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride had a candid conversation about their game and team recently. On the show’s page, an Instagram clip featured Kolek answering the question, “Who is the fakest celebrity Knicks fan?” He said, “At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative, ’cause, like, they just want to be seen at the game. They’re not necessarily fans. Maybe Taylor Swift?” Agreeing with Kolek, McBride added, “Swifties not going to like that answer.” Both players realized that the global sensation’s fans might give them “some hate” over their response. Furthermore, McBride explained that other celebrities like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan are “solid” fans. Adding to that, his fellow player said, “I guess she’s got a lot going on, so she can’t come all the time.” This made McBride chuckle as he admitted Kolek was trying to save himself from online backlash. However, the 25-year-old NBA star insisted that Swift was a “bit performative” with her attendance. Meanwhile, the video has garnered over 5K likes as of this writing. Many users agreed with the two players’ opinion that Swift is a fake fan. But some also supported the Grammy winner, arguing she has been into the Knicks for a long time. Swift was last spotted at a New York Knicks game on June 10, 2026. It was Game 4 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden. Interestingly, the next month, she got married at the same venue to Travis Kelce. The post Knicks Star Calls Taylor Swift Their ‘Fakest Fan’ With ‘Performative’ Dig — Source appeared first on Reality Tea .

item.title: Blue Jays predicted to sign $10M ex-Yankees veteran, Silver Slugger winner to replace Ernie Clement
item.description: Blue Jays predicted to sign $10M ex-Yankees veteran, Silver Slugger winner to replace Ernie Clement originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays enter another offseason with several areas to address, especially after a disappointing season. Coming off a World Series appearance, Toronto struggled to maintain that success and fell short of expectations. Injuries and inconsistency made for a difficult season. This offseason, the Blue Jays could look to add another infielder to strengthen their roster. “The infield largely remains the same. Toronto hopes for a bounce-back season from Guerrero Jr., while Clement and Gimenez are up the middle, and Okamoto stays at the hot corner. The Blue Jays could add another low-cost infielder this offseason," SI's Zion Trammell wrote. Ernie Clement struggled during the second half of the season and could be better suited for a utility role rather than playing one position every day. CBS Sports’ Mike Axisa believes that moving Clement around the infield could open the door for Toronto to pursue Jazz Chisholm Jr. “Ernie Clement crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility guy who moves around rather than someone who plays one set position every day. The Blue Jays desperately need a power infusion, particularly from the left side of the plate, and Chisholm's defense and baserunning will fit in nicely as well. I wonder if any teams would show interest in Chisholm at third base or center field, two positions he's played in the past. Second base in Toronto is my best guess for now,” Axisa wrote. Although Chisholm has reportedly expressed interest in returning to the Bronx, a reunion with the Yankees may not be likely. “As the Yankees look to retool their roster for the 2027 season, there's a massive hole they will need to fill. Second base, manned by Jazz Chisholm Jr. for the last two seasons, will explore free agency and it's likely he will not return to the Bronx," SNY's Phillip Martinez wrote. The Blue Jays would be adding a player from a division rival who could make an impact in several areas of the lineup. Additionally, Chisholm's limited playing time during the postseason could give him extra motivation heading into 2027, particularly when facing the Yankees. Chisholm played under a $10.2 million contract with New York in 2026. His upside remains considerable, and after a somewhat disappointing season, he could be motivated to make a major impact in 2027. item.title: Barcelona prepare emergency January signing as Flick demands defensive reinforcement
item.description: Barcelona prepare emergency January signing as Flick demands defensive reinforcement According to an update from SPORT , it has come to light that Barcelona are preparing to strengthen their defence during the January transfer window, with Hansi Flick keen to bring in another centre-back. The Catalan side is exploring ways to increase their financial flexibility, but their restricted spending capacity means they will have to consider alternative transfer arrangements. As such, the need for defensive reinforcements has become increasingly apparent following a series of injuries and disappointing results against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid. With several months remaining in the campaign, Barcelona are concerned about their ability to maintain defensive depth during a demanding second half of the season, which is why they are thinking of making an emergency signing. Flick pushes Barcelona towards January defensive signing Barcelona’s transfer plans have gained urgency following the problems experienced in recent weeks. Injuries to Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and then Xavi Espart have disrupted Flick’s defensive options, exposing the lack of reliable alternatives in defence when several first-team players are unavailable. Barcelona could make an emergency January signing. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The consecutive defeats against PSG and Real Madrid have further highlighted those weaknesses, with the coaching staff increasingly aware that the existing defensive resources could become insufficient as the fixture schedule intensifies. As a result, Barcelona are now working towards finding a centre-back capable of delivering an immediate improvement rather than simply recruiting a prospect for the future. Barcelona’s financial restrictions complicate transfer plans For now, Financial considerations remain the biggest obstacle to completing a deal. As previously reported, Barcelona currently have a financial fair play margin of approximately €3–4 million , leaving limited room for another significant commitment. The club cannot comfortably accommodate an expensive transfer fee alongside the corresponding salary obligations of an established defender. Consequently, a loan agreement could become an attractive solution, allowing Barcelona to reinforce their squad without assuming the full financial burden of a permanent acquisition immediately. Flick wants to add a new central defender. What is Barcelona’s plan? At present, Barcelona are examining two different recruitment approaches. Ultimately, though, the January decision will depend on financial flexibility, player availability and whether the right opportunity emerges.

item.title: Real Madrid’s Bernardo Silva pays emotional tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo following international retirement: ‘An inspiration to us all
item.description: Real Madrid’s Bernardo Silva pays emotional tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo following international retirement: ‘An inspiration to us all Real Madrid legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced yesterday that he was hanging up his boots for Portugal, bringing the curtain down on a glorious international career. The announcement has naturally struck a chord at Los Blancos , a club that has celebrated the veteran striker for years. Among those paying tribute is Real Madrid star Bernardo Silva, who has shared a dressing room with Ronaldo for years. Bernardo Silva pays tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo Taking to Instagram, Silva shared a photograph of himself embracing Ronaldo in the Portugal shirt, accompanied by a heartfelt message expressing his gratitude. “It was undoubtedly a great honor and pleasure to have played alongside you for so many years! You are an inspiration to us all. Thank you very much for everything, Cristiano,” he wrote. The message comes after Ronaldo brought his 23-year international career to a close. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bernardo Carvalho E Silva (@bernardocarvalhosilva) The 41-year-old leaves the international stage with a mind-boggling 146 goals in 234 appearances, both world records in men’s football. He also captained Portugal to their first Euros title in 2016 and Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025. A legacy that transcends boundaries Regardless of where their allegiances lie, the football world will come together to bid farewell to a player who has left such a lasting impact on the game. What a career Ronaldo has had with Portugal. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) To borrow a very famous phrase from Mike Tyson, “every head must bow, every tongue must confess, this is the greatest of all time” . For Real Madrid supporters, Ronaldo’s international retirement brings back glorious memories of his time in the Spanish capital. Between 2009 and 2018, the Portuguese superstar scored an astonishing 451 goals in 438 competitive appearances for Los Blancos . He helped the team secure four Champions League titles. Bernardo Silva may not have crossed paths with Ronaldo at Madrid, but he will be happy to be playing for the club now. His tribute shows how much his teammates respected and continue to respect Ronaldo, and fans will now tune in to Al Nassr matches to keep watching him play for as long as possible.

item.title: Bullem takes over as C’River PDP Chairman
item.description: …as Party Backs Wike’s Rainbow Coalition By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Cross River State has ratified Chief Francis Bullem as its substantive State Chairman, while pledging loyalty to its national leader and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Mr Nyesom Wike, and endorsing his Rainbow Coalition. The decisions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the party’s State Executive Committee, SEC, meeting held on Thursday at the party’s State Secretariat in Calabar. The communiqué, signed by the State Publicity Secretary, Mr Mike Ojisi, said the SEC acknowledged and accepted the resignation of the former State Chairman, Mr Venatius Ikem. It said the committee approved Bullem’s nomination and subsequently ratified him as substantive chairman in line with Article 47, Sections 5 and 6 of the PDP Constitution (2017), as amended. Vanguard gathered that the development is expected to usher in a new leadership phase for the party in the state. The SEC also endorsed the Rainbow Coalition led by Wike, a former Rivers State governor, describing him as the party’s national leader. The endorsement signals the state chapter’s support for the political platform he leads. The committee expressed concern over what it described as incessant attacks on PDP members and members of other opposition parties while carrying out legitimate political activities across the state. It condemned the attacks and reaffirmed its commitment to protecting the rights of party members to participate freely in lawful political activities. The communiqué stressed the need for an atmosphere in which political parties and their members could operate without intimidation or harassment. The SEC reiterated its commitment to the party’s constitutional provisions and political activities in Cross River. It would be recalled that Ikem resigned from the PDP on October 16, citing internal divisions, a crisis of direction and leadership incoherence within the party. The post Bullem takes over as C’River PDP Chairman appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lamine Yamal takes Mbappé’s Champions League under-20 scoring record as Barça beat Villa 3-0
item.description: Lamine Yamal takes Mbappé’s Champions League under-20 scoring record as Barça beat Villa 3-0 Lamine Yamal became the Champions League's top scorer before the age of 20 as Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, taking the mark from Kylian Mbappé. The record comes soon after Mbappé's double decided the Clásico, and the win lifts Barça to second in the league phase. Lamine Yamal has taken a Champions League scoring record from Kylian Mbappé. He opened the scoring in Barcelona’s win over Aston Villa at Spotify Camp Nou on 3 November. A Villa mistake in the seventh minute gave him the chance. Yamal curled the ball past goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. That goal was his 14th in the competition. No player has scored more before turning 20. Mbappé had managed 13 at that age. The Real Madrid forward now has 72 Champions League goals in total. The timing gives the record an edge. Mbappé scored in the 41st and 87th minutes as Real Madrid won the season’s first Clásico 2-1 at Spotify Camp Nou on 25 October. Raphinha’s 61st-minute goal was Barcelona’s only reply that night. Yamal still has until July to extend the mark Yamal needed 37 Champions League appearances to reach his total. He does not turn 20 until next July. The record could therefore grow further this season. The two forwards had been level at an earlier stage, each with 10 Champions League goals before their 19th birthdays, according to FC Barcelona. Raphinha did the rest against Villa. He made it 2-0 in the 52nd minute and struck again 12 minutes later. His double moved him alongside Ronaldinho in Barça’s scoring list. It also lifted his tally for the season to 19 goals in 13 games. The club’s match report named him MVP. Goalkeeper Joan García was picked out as the standout player of the first half. Clean win lifts Barcelona to second behind PSG The result matters for the table as much as the record books. Barcelona came into the game after a 4-2 defeat to PSG. A clean sheet and three goals restored some calm. The win also ended Villa’s perfect start. The English side had won all three of their earlier league-phase games. This was their first Champions League defeat of the season. Aston Villa said it was their first meeting with Barcelona since their two-legged Super Cup win in January 1983. Barcelona now sit second. Only PSG, with four wins from four, are above them. Villa have the same points total but trail on goal difference. The league phase runs until 27 January 2027. Attention now turns to LaLiga. Barcelona visit second-placed Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano on 8 November in a matchday-12 fixture kicking off at 9pm CET. The international break follows. Barcelona then return at home to Villarreal on 22 November. Sources Lamine Yamal top Champions League scorer under 20 years of age (FC Barcelona) FC Barcelona vs Real Madrid (LaLiga) 2026/27 Champions League: All the league phase fixtures and results (UEFA) Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa (Aston Villa FC)

item.title: Ravens RB Derrick Henry instantly shuts down trade noise after Jaguars rout
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Ravens RB Derrick Henry instantly shuts down trade noise after Jaguars rout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens suffered another ugly loss on Thursday night, this time falling 33-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium . Amid growing chatter about his future, the star running back made it clear he is not thinking about going anywhere . Henry was asked after the game whether he expects to remain with the team for the rest of the season, given Baltimore’s struggles. He quickly shut down the idea . “I’m not mentioning me going anywhere else. I’m saying let’s go back to work, try to get better and turn this around,” Henry said, via Cordell Woodland. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The question came after ESPN’s Dan Graziano flagged Henry as “someone to keep an eye on” ahead of the trade deadline. The 32-year-old turns 33 in January and is set to earn $12 million next season, none of which is guaranteed. It has been a frustrating stretch for Henry and the Ravens. Baltimore has now lost four straight games, dropping to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North. Injuries have played a major role, with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley landing on injured reserve. That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his first career start on just three days’ rest, and he completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with two interceptions. Henry’s own struggles continued. He finished with 57 yards on 17 carries and took 10 direct snaps, marking his fourth straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill provided Baltimore’s lone touchdown with a 65-yard run in the fourth quarter, with the game already out of reach. Still, Henry made some history in the loss. He passed both Jerome Bettis and LaDainian Tomlinson to move into seventh place on the NFL’s all-time rushing list , with Curtis Martin next in his sights. Meanwhile, the Jaguars improved to 6-2 behind a balanced effort. Trevor Lawrence connected with Parker Washington on a 50-yard touchdown before halftime, and Cam Little knocked down four field goals. The Ravens will have extra time to regroup before hosting the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football on Nov. 16. Henry’s comments suggest he wants to be part of the turnaround, but Baltimore’s front office could face some tough decisions if the losing continues. Related: Ravens’ Mark Andrews is completely unfazed after getting booed by home fans Related: What Ravens’ Joe Fagnano said after getting pummeled by Jaguars in first NFL start

item.title: From street fighter to world champion - Bentley's rise to top
item.description: Denzel Bentley has 18 wins by knockout in his 22 victories [Getty Images] Denzel Bentley was supposed to be fighting for a world title. Instead, he was close to becoming a delivery driver. Having ended 2024 on a high by winning the British middleweight title for a third time and adding the European crown to his collection, Bentley, 31, had every reason to believe a world title fight would be next. Meetings with promoter Queensberry offered Bentley hope until fight cards were announced and promises were broken. During his time in the wilderness, Londoner Bentley was left with a dwindling bank account - leading him to look at new ways to earn money to stay afloat. Without a fight purse to rely on, a chance conversation with his cousin almost saw Bentley taking up the role of a delivery driver. "After a year out, I thought I needed to do something," Bentley told BBC Sport. "I'm not bad with my money and was able to hold myself up to that point but it was starting to bite. My cousin said download the Amazon app and you can get a zero-hour contract. It was an app where you could check in and see if there was delivery work in your area. "I downloaded it and signed in but there were no jobs in my area. I remember always refreshing and checking but there were no jobs in my area - that's the only reason I didn't do it." Becoming world champion and being stripped without fighting Bentley's 16-month absence from the ring did count for something when he captured the WBO interim middleweight title by overcoming Endry Saavedra in April 2026. And three months later he was elevated to full world champion status following Janibek Alimkhanuly's decision to move up to super-middleweight. Finally Bentley had achieved his lifelong goal. But his reign lasted just 102 days, in which he made no defences, after he agreed to face Shane Mosely Jr rather than face his mandatory challenger. Bentley, who fights the American at London's Copper Box Arena on Saturday, admitted frustration over the decision but believes promoter Zuffa Boxing can get him back in the world title mix. "I've moved over to Zuffa and everyone thinks it's a money move," Bentley said. "Firstly, I do want to get compensated rightly for the job I have - it's a demanding job and we take a lot of punches. "But I want to become world champion again. All of the above can be true, I don't have to sacrifice one for the other. I've asked Zuffa to get me back in position to win another one. They said no problem." 'Game-changer' bikes to the gym Denzel Bentley made his professional debut in 2017 [Getty Images] Bentley's introduction to boxing was rather unconventional - a fight club run by his brother on his local estate. A headguard, gloves and a friend were all that were needed for Bentley - who boasts a record of 22 wins, three losses and one draw - to have his first taste of the sport. item.content:encoded: Denzel Bentley has 18 wins by knockout in his 22 victories [Getty Images] Denzel Bentley was supposed to be fighting for a world title. Instead, he was close to becoming a delivery driver. Having ended 2024 on a high by winning the British middleweight title for a third time and adding the European crown to his collection, Bentley, 31, had every reason to believe a world title fight would be next. Meetings with promoter Queensberry offered Bentley hope until fight cards were announced and promises were broken. During his time in the wilderness, Londoner Bentley was left with a dwindling bank account - leading him to look at new ways to earn money to stay afloat. Without a fight purse to rely on, a chance conversation with his cousin almost saw Bentley taking up the role of a delivery driver. "After a year out, I thought I needed to do something," Bentley told BBC Sport. "I'm not bad with my money and was able to hold myself up to that point but it was starting to bite. My cousin said download the Amazon app and you can get a zero-hour contract. It was an app where you could check in and see if there was delivery work in your area. "I downloaded it and signed in but there were no jobs in my area. I remember always refreshing and checking but there were no jobs in my area - that's the only reason I didn't do it." Becoming world champion and being stripped without fighting Bentley's 16-month absence from the ring did count for something when he captured the WBO interim middleweight title by overcoming Endry Saavedra in April 2026. And three months later he was elevated to full world champion status following Janibek Alimkhanuly's decision to move up to super-middleweight. Finally Bentley had achieved his lifelong goal. But his reign lasted just 102 days, in which he made no defences, after he agreed to face Shane Mosely Jr rather than face his mandatory challenger. Bentley, who fights the American at London's Copper Box Arena on Saturday, admitted frustration over the decision but believes promoter Zuffa Boxing can get him back in the world title mix. "I've moved over to Zuffa and everyone thinks it's a money move," Bentley said. "Firstly, I do want to get compensated rightly for the job I have - it's a demanding job and we take a lot of punches. "But I want to become world champion again. All of the above can be true, I don't have to sacrifice one for the other. I've asked Zuffa to get me back in position to win another one. They said no problem." 'Game-changer' bikes to the gym Denzel Bentley made his professional debut in 2017 [Getty Images] Bentley's introduction to boxing was rather unconventional - a fight club run by his brother on his local estate. A headguard, gloves and a friend were all that were needed for Bentley - who boasts a record of 22 wins, three losses and one draw - to have his first taste of the sport. But he soon realised that boxing in the streets was a lot different from the real thing. "When I went to college, I met a friend who boxed and because of what I'd been doing in the streets with my brother, I said, 'yeah, I can box too'," Bentley said. "But I found out it was really different. I remember calling the punches the wrong names. I thought it was left jab, right jab, but it's obviously a jab and a right hand or a cross. "I was hitting the bags but had the wrong form and then I was getting battered in sparring. I thought 'OK, this wasn't what I was doing' but I wanted to learn how to do it." And then getting to the gym came with its own problems, but nothing the inventive Bentley couldn't get around with the help of Santander bikes. "I was short on money, had sold my car and didn't really want to spend money on buses. I would rent out the Santander bikes," Bentley said. "I would put in £2 and pace down the road to make sure I didn't take more than 30 minutes and then park up and come home. It wouldn't charge me extra as long as I never went over half an hour. "Before that, I would walk to the gym. I lived in Battersea and the gym was in Bermondsey. "I'd just put my music in and people would ask, 'Oh, you like walking to the gym?' but I just didn't have any other choice. When I discovered the bikes, it was a game-changer." item.title: ‘Been cheating’- Chiefs fans face fiery response over Patrick Mahomes and controversial call
item.description: Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Former Denver Broncos safety Justin Simmons has hit back at Kansas City Chiefs fans questioning the controversial false start call that helped decide their team’s defeat. The Chiefs appeared to have snatched a late victory against Denver after Patrick Mahomes found the end zone in the final seconds. However, a false start penalty on Jaylon Moore wiped out the touchdown before Kansas City eventually lost 28-24. Chiefs supporters were quick to question the decision, but Simmons has little sympathy for their complaints and believes the officials made the right call. Justin Simmons accuses Kansas City Chiefs of benefiting from refereeing decisions Speaking on DNVR Sports’ The Last Line with J.Simms + K. Jack , Simmons launched into a fiery response to the criticism from Kansas City fans. He said: “I seen it all on social media and I already got beef with Chiefs fans anyway. That wasn’t a false start. They call that on us. They hate us… My rant? Y’all been cheating y’all whole time y’all had Patrick Mahomes. That’s my rant. Refs been cheating for y’all.” Simmons also took issue with the amount of attention Mahomes receives, even when the Chiefs are not playing. “I’m watching Sunday Night Football when I hear, ‘You know, this guy reminds me of? Number 15 in Kansas City, Patrick Mahomes.’ And we’re not even watching the Chiefs. We’re watching the New York Giants versus the Dallas Cowboys. And I gotta hear about Patrick Mahomes.” He then doubled down on his criticism of the fanbase, insisting the penalty was justified. “My rant is at the Chiefs fans that are delusional enough to think that that was not a false start. It was. Y’all lost. And y’all lost at the one-yard line. Ha!” The controversy centred on Moore moving his right foot after turning his head to look at Mahomes. A Broncos linebacker pointed out the movement, and officials ruled it a false start. Head coach Andy Reid disagreed with the decision, while Mahomes admitted he had not seen the replay but accepted the officials’ call. However, Simmons and former Broncos teammate Kareem Jackson have both defended the referees. For Kansas City, the missed opportunity proved costly, with Malcolm Roach sacking Mahomes on the ensuing fourth-down attempt to seal Denver’s 28-24 win. item.title: South Africa's ANC party on track to face 'nightmare' losses in municipal elections
item.description: South Africa's African National Congress party could face its worst-ever election result on Friday, with early counting suggesting it received only 32% ‌of the vote in the country’s municipal elections. Over two-thirds of votes have been counted so far, and the final results are expected later in the day.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Braves predicted to sign $75M ex-Yankees three-time All-Star, wins leader to pair with Chris Sale
item.description: Braves predicted to sign $75M ex-Yankees three-time All-Star, wins leader to pair with Chris Sale originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves have dealt with the same problem for several years when it comes to things going wrong during a season. Atlanta entered 2026 with a solid pitching staff, but injuries once again derailed the rotation. Heading into the trade deadline, the Braves didn't have a reliable second arm behind Chris Sale. It was an issue that was apparent to everyone. “There are well-documented reasons why the Braves were in the market for a frontline starter at the Trade Deadline. Though they added a depth piece in Tyler Mahle, they didn't land the type of clear difference-maker that many fans wanted. As the team heads down the stretch, there's now even more scrutiny on a few things: the lack of a potent 1-2 punch for the postseason, their bullpen's durability and the rotation's overall dependability," MLB.com's Jason Foster wrote. Now, heading into 2027, Atlanta faces similar questions about the stability of its pitching rotation. “While it wasn't their downfall in the end, the starting rotation has been a constant thorn in the Atlanta Braves' side for multiple seasons now. For 2026, it was no different. As the page turns to 2027, it's to see how it shakes up. There will be at least one guarantee. Chris Sale is the ace. You probably guarantee that Bryce Elder is in the mix, too, along with Grant Holmes. After that, we'll see what happens," SI's Harrison Smajovitts wrote. With the Braves needing another frontline arm, Sports Illustrated’s Will Laws believes they will pursue Sonny Gray. “Not many pitchers of Gray’s age can command a multi-year deal, but he might just do it after recording a 2.72 ERA for the Red Sox and leading MLB in wins (18). Gray is dependable as they come, being one of just six pitchers to hurl at least 160 innings in each of the last four seasons. The wily veteran has shown a propensity for pitching in a variety of different environments, and though his strikeout numbers shrank last season, he hasn’t logged a below-average FIP since 2016. The question is when Father Time will catch up with him,” Laws wrote. Gray was dominant in 2026, leading all of MLB with 18 wins. The right-hander has pitched for several teams throughout his career, including the New York Yankees . Gray recently completed his $75 million contract with the Boston Red Sox. The Braves have seemingly been linked to him around previous trade deadlines, and now they could have an opportunity to bring the successful right-hander to Atlanta in free agency. item.title: Former Vanderbilt Star Diego Pavia Receives Strong Ravens Endorsement From Skip Bayless
item.description: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Diego Pavia. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 28: Diego Pavia of the Vanderbilt Commodores throws a pass during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 28, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Former Vanderbilt Commodores quarterback Diego Pavia might not currently have an NFL job, but that certainly hasn’t stopped longtime sports personality Skip Bayless from believing he belongs on the field. With the Baltimore Ravens facing the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, Bayless made a bold declaration regarding the former Heisman Trophy finalist. He believes Baltimore would have a better chance of winning with Pavia under center, despite the organization releasing him earlier this year. “If Diego Pavia were starting tonight at QB for the Ravens, they’d have a much better chance of winning,” Bayless said on Thursday. The statement carries additional significance considering Baltimore actually signed Pavia following the 2026 NFL Draft. Unfortunately for the former Vanderbilt standout, his opportunity with the franchise ended before training camp. Skip Bayless Questions Ravens’ Decision on Diego Pavia Baltimore signed Pavia as an undrafted free agent in April, giving the former SEC star an opportunity to compete for a roster spot. However, the Ravens waived him July 23, ultimately moving forward with other quarterbacks. That decision looks particularly interesting now that Baltimore is dealing with significant injuries at the position. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – FEBRUARY 28: Diego Pavia of the Vanderbilt Commodores throws a pass during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 28, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley were both placed on injured reserve after suffering injuries against the Buffalo Bills . Consequently, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was tasked with starting Thursday’s matchup against Jacksonville. Fagnano also played during Baltimore’s 36-10 loss to Buffalo, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards while throwing an interception. Bayless clearly believes the Ravens overlooked an opportunity when they moved on from Pavia. Diego Pavia’s Vanderbilt Success Still Commands Attention Pavia’s collegiate accomplishments provide some context for Bayless’ confidence. During his final season at Vanderbilt, the quarterback helped lead the Commodores to their first 10-win campaign while finishing second in the Heisman Trophy voting. He completed 70% of his passes, threw 29 touchdowns and demonstrated the improvisational ability that made him one of college football’s most entertaining players. Unfortunately for the former Vanderbilt standout, his opportunity with the franchise ended before training camp. Skip Bayless Questions Ravens’ Decision on Diego Pavia Baltimore signed Pavia as an undrafted free agent in April, giving the former SEC star an opportunity to compete for a roster spot. However, the Ravens waived him July 23, ultimately moving forward with other quarterbacks. That decision looks particularly interesting now that Baltimore is dealing with significant injuries at the position. Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA – FEBRUARY 28: Diego Pavia of the Vanderbilt Commodores throws a pass during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 28, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley were both placed on injured reserve after suffering injuries against the Buffalo Bills . Consequently, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was tasked with starting Thursday’s matchup against Jacksonville. Fagnano also played during Baltimore’s 36-10 loss to Buffalo, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards while throwing an interception. Bayless clearly believes the Ravens overlooked an opportunity when they moved on from Pavia. Diego Pavia’s Vanderbilt Success Still Commands Attention Pavia’s collegiate accomplishments provide some context for Bayless’ confidence. During his final season at Vanderbilt, the quarterback helped lead the Commodores to their first 10-win campaign while finishing second in the Heisman Trophy voting. He completed 70% of his passes, threw 29 touchdowns and demonstrated the improvisational ability that made him one of college football’s most entertaining players. However, questions surrounding his size and transition to professional football contributed to his uncertain NFL future. Pavia has since expressed interest in continuing his career through the United Football League, keeping the possibility of another professional opportunity alive. Whether he would actually outperform Baltimore’s current quarterbacks remains impossible to establish without seeing him compete against NFL defenses. Nevertheless, Bayless’ endorsement illustrates how strongly some observers still believe in the former Vanderbilt star. For Pavia, watching his former NFL team navigate a quarterback crisis only makes his absence more fascinating. His college career proved he could overcome considerable doubt, but earning another NFL opportunity remains the next challenge. Adding to Bayless’ analysis, the Ravens rookie quarterback struggled to generate offense during Thursday night’s matchup against the Jaguars. That still doesn’t mean Pavia would have fared any better. It certainly would have made tremendous television. item.title: ‘Get (Kirk) Herbstreit Off My TV,’ ‘Trying So Hard to Fake Interest’ — NFL Fans Rip Veteran Broadcaster’s ‘Irritating’ Commentary on Jaguars-Ravens
item.description: Jan 18, 2026; Miami, FL, USA; ESPN College GameDay analyst Kirk Herbstreit speaks to fans at fan fest in the Miami Beach Convention Center before the College Football National Championship between the Indiana Hoosiers and the Miami Hurricanes in Miami Florida. © Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Thursday night turned into a long one for more than just the Baltimore Ravens. The Jacksonville Jaguars rolled to a 33-10 win at M&T Bank Stadium, holding undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to 10-of-18 passing for 60 yards with two interceptions in his first NFL start. But as the game dragged on, fans took aim at Prime Video analyst Kirk Herbstreit for several reasons. One fan even wanted Herbstreit off the broadcast altogether, while several others took issue with his “fake interest” in a game that was lopsided from the jump. NFL Fans Call Out Kirk Herbstreit’s “Irritating” Commentary on TNF Herbstreit called the game as the analyst beside Al Michaels. The Ravens came in on a three-game losing streak and turned to Fagnano after losing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in Buffalo. As the night wore on, one fan minced no words about the quality of the broadcast. “Get Herbstreit off my TV,” the viewer wrote, referring to Herbstreit’s comments on Fagnano’s wife, Lydia, when he said, “His wife may have a postgame breakdown in the kitchen.” Earlier, Herbstreit also noted that Lydia had been helping Joe prepare by running walkthroughs in their living room and reading plays to him. Meanwhile, another complaint came down to the basics of commentary. “Kirk Herbstreit is getting paid $20 million a year to call football games, but he can’t pronounce the word ‘Jaguars’ correctly. So irritating,” a fan wrote. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer The criticism went beyond delivery to the booth pairing itself. “I’ll state once again: Kirk Herbstreit is stealing money from Amazon; he adds nothing to the TNF NFL broadcast,” a fan wrote. How Herbstreit came across beside Michaels caught another fan’s eye as well: “Kirk Herbstreit looks like he’s trying so hard to fake interest in whatever Al Michaels is talking about right now.” Michaels did not escape criticism entirely, though, as another fan went after both men and the state of the game: “I will be staying up until 11:30 ET to hate watch the Ravens in a blowout, with Al Michaels talking about who knows what and Kirk Herbstreit providing derisive, uninformed, passive-aggressive comments about analytics.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Coming back to the game, after Jake Moody’s 53-yard field goal pulled the Ravens within 7-3 in the first quarter, the Jaguars scored the next 26 points, 12 of them on Cam Little field goals, and all three of Baltimore’s turnovers came after halftime. item.title: Ireland vs Argentina offers tantalising World Cup preview to kick off huge autumn
item.description: World Cup quarter-final. Six syllables to chill the bones of any Ireland rugby fan. A peak seemingly so impossible to summit that it makes Mount Everest look like Slieve Donard. Ireland’s dismal record in rugby’s global showpiece scarcely needs repeating – but we’ll do so anyway. In the 10 editions of the World Cup to date, the Irish have been knocked out in the quarter-finals a ludicrous eight times, the short-lived quarter-final play-off once and the pool stage once. They simply cannot reach the semi-finals. It doesn’t matter whether they enter as a plucky underdog (1987 – lost 33-15 to Australia) or the No 1-ranked side in the world (2019 – beaten 46-14 by New Zealand ); whether they’ve downed a southern hemisphere giant to top their pool (2023 – lost 28-24 to the All Blacks after 37 phases of agony ) or have scraped through the groups in second spot (1995 – lost 36-12 to France), the result is the same. Ireland have endured World Cup heartbreak time and time again (PA) Sometimes it’s one-sided (2003 – beaten 43-21 by Les Bleus, having trailed 27-0 at half-time) and sometimes it’s agonising (1991 – lost 19-18 to Australia thanks to Michael Lynagh’s 80th-minute try in the corner) but it’s always a last-eight exit. But why are we talking about Ireland’s World Cup wobbles when there is almost a year to go until the latest edition in Australia? Because the very first game of this autumn’s Nations Championship is set to give us a tantalising preview of what could be to come in 12 months’ time. If everything goes to seeding (a big if, granted..), with both teams topping their pool and negotiating an eminently winnable last-16 clash, then on 31 October 2027 in Brisbane, Ireland and Argentina will do battle in a Rugby World Cup quarter-final. And this Friday night in Dublin, those same teams will try lay down a psychological marker, while kickstarting their autumn in style. Joe McCarthy scored a try when Ireland won the last game between the sides in 2024 (PA) Juan Cruz Mallia is one of Argentina’s game-breaking options (PA) Ireland will be confident. After a 36-14 defeat in Paris to begin the 2026 Six Nations, they reeled off four straight wins to finish second in the table, and only missed out on the title due to Thomas Ramos’s 83rd-minute penalty against England on Super Saturday, before beating Australia and Japan away from home in the summer. The northern hemisphere table in the Nations Championship looks wide open, with four teams tied on two wins from three so far and all will fancy their chances of topping the pile and reaching the final later this month, although the match against the double world champion Springboks in a fortnight’s time looms large for Ireland. A trio of key men will be returning to the starting line-up against Los Pumas after missing a year worth of international matches – loosehead prop Andrew Porter, flanker Ryan Baird and wing Mack Hansen – while 23-year-old fly half Sam Prendergast has recovered sufficiently from a wri

But why are we talking about Ireland’s World Cup wobbles when there is almost a year to go until the latest edition in Australia? Because the very first game of this autumn’s Nations Championship is set to give us a tantalising preview of what could be to come in 12 months’ time. If everything goes to seeding (a big if, granted..), with both teams topping their pool and negotiating an eminently winnable last-16 clash, then on 31 October 2027 in Brisbane, Ireland and Argentina will do battle in a Rugby World Cup quarter-final. And this Friday night in Dublin, those same teams will try lay down a psychological marker, while kickstarting their autumn in style. Joe McCarthy scored a try when Ireland won the last game between the sides in 2024 (PA) Juan Cruz Mallia is one of Argentina’s game-breaking options (PA) Ireland will be confident. After a 36-14 defeat in Paris to begin the 2026 Six Nations, they reeled off four straight wins to finish second in the table, and only missed out on the title due to Thomas Ramos’s 83rd-minute penalty against England on Super Saturday, before beating Australia and Japan away from home in the summer. The northern hemisphere table in the Nations Championship looks wide open, with four teams tied on two wins from three so far and all will fancy their chances of topping the pile and reaching the final later this month, although the match against the double world champion Springboks in a fortnight’s time looms large for Ireland. A trio of key men will be returning to the starting line-up against Los Pumas after missing a year worth of international matches – loosehead prop Andrew Porter, flanker Ryan Baird and wing Mack Hansen – while 23-year-old fly half Sam Prendergast has recovered sufficiently from a wrist injury to wear the No 10 jersey. Prendergast’s fitness is a boost but, truthfully, Ireland are still yet to truly nail down Johnny Sexton’s long-term successor in the position and Jack Crowley being ruled out with a vascular issue in his leg is a blow. Sam Prendergast is fit to start for Ireland at fly-half (PA) Similarly, the absence of injured captain Caelan Doris hurts, although New Zealand-born thumper Sean Jansen has impressed for Connacht in the past couple of seasons and scored a try off the bench on his Ireland debut against Japan in the summer. This autumn is a golden opportunity for the 27-year-old to cement himself as Doris’s primary backup at No 8 and secure a spot in the first-choice 23 moving forward. Head coach Andy Farrell is building nicely towards the World Cup and an excellent historical record against Argentina will only buoy him further. Los Pumas have never beaten Ireland on Irish soil (although did down the British and Irish Lions at the Aviva Stadium last summer) and have lost 14 of the 20 total games between the sides. Their head coach Felipe Contepomi remains a cult hero in parts of the Emerald Isle thanks to a scintillating six-year spell with Leinster during his playing days and they have game-breaking talent dotted throughout the side, most notably in a fearsome back row consisting of Pablo Matera, Marcos Kremer and Juan Martin Gonzalez. Felipe Contepomi is a club legend at Leinster (Getty) A disappointing summer saw them beat only Wales, while losing to England, Scotland, Australia and all-conquering South Africa but the hiring of defensive guru Shaun Edwards as defence coach has made waves. How good Edwards’ Spanish is remains unclear but the Wigan native’s intensity has always been conveyed through more than just words and his coaching style appears to transcend language. It’s 11 years since the Pumas last gave Ireland a bloody nose but perhaps they should simply pretend this is a World Cup match. Because of the six victories they’ve registered against the men in green, exactly half have come in do-or-die contests at rugby’s most prestigious tournament. They won the unnecessarily convoluted quarter-final play-off 28-24 to knock Ireland out in 1999, a 30-15 triumph in 2007 sent a Brian O’Driscoll-led outfit packing in the pool stage and a 43-20 quarter-final shellacking ended the 2015 Irish vintage’s hopes of finally tasting a semi-final. Some of Ireland’s darkest, most heart-wrenching rugby days have been authored by snarling Pumas. Argentina broke Irish hearts in the 2015 World Cup quarter-final (Getty) If the pair do meet in the World Cup last eight next year, the match will – fittingly – be played on Halloween. At this point, the narrative frankly writes itself, with the ghosts of all Ireland’s past failures needing to be exorcised on the day made to fuel nightmares. But for now, we get an intriguing preview and the teams have a chance to earn a psychological advantage before that prospective clash. The game suddenly has an added significance for an Ireland side that could do with every bit of assistance possible as they prepare to scale the World Cup mountain and a win would be another hurdle successfully negotiated.
