item.title: Colts rumors: Jonathan Taylor ‘expects to be traded,’ insider claims
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Colts rumors: Jonathan Taylor ‘expects to be traded,’ insider claims appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jonathan Taylor watched the Indianapolis Colts trade left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner hours apart. He probably caught glimpse of a team social media post that was hyping up rookie running back Seth McGowan on that same day. He also knows that the organization is undergoing changes after firing general manager Chris Ballard. The franchise has done everything to signal that a rebuild is underway, except ship out No. 28. Most fans anticipate that he too will switch teams before the Nov. 10 deadline, and apparently, so does the player himself. “My understanding is Jonathan Taylor expects to be traded,” insider James Palmer said on the NFL on Prime Video postgame show Thursday night. “We’ll see if somebody gets up {to the Colts’ high asking price}.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) What's the latest on Jonathan Taylor heading into the weekend? My report on our @NFLonPrime postgame show. pic.twitter.com/nmW4l3Xdcm — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) November 6, 2026 Palmer listed the Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants, Green Bay Packers and Denver Broncos as suitors. There have been offers, but Indianapolis is currently not satisfied with the packages that are being presented. Nonetheless, Taylor is bracing himself for a change of scenery. The 27-year-old is a former All-Pro who has led the NFL in rushing yards once and rushing touchdowns twice. He is the Colts’ all-time leader in the latter category (77 TDs) and ranks second behind Edgerrin James in the former (8,208). The body of work is undeniably impressive, hence why Indy is seeking significant value in return. But is a decline coming? Taylor is averaging an adequate yet unspectacular 4.1 yards per rushing attempt this season. While he is still dangerous with the ball in his hands, one has to wonder if this efficiency dip is only the beginning. Back-to-back seasons with 300-plus carries are bound to take a toll on a man. Playoff-caliber squads clearly still covet his skill set, however. Taylor is preparing for Sunday’s meeting with the visiting Dallas Cowboys, but he is perfectly aware of the prominent place he occupies in the rumor mill . The No. 41 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft is exercising common sense ahead of the trade deadline. Taylor has amassed 812 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns through eight games played. Related: Colts’ Daniel Jones still promises to ‘cut it loose’ vs. Cowboys despite benching rumors getting louder Related: Colts’ Josh Downs speaks up on awkward situation after trade request

(Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Getty On Friday, the Los Angeles Lakers get a shot at redemption as they take on the Portland Trail Blazers in the 2026 NBA Cup. The Lakers suffered their first loss of the season against the Blazers on October 27. They are also looking to get their first cup win of the campaign. Another loss for the Lakers in the NBA Cup further hurts their chances of advancing to the knockout stages. Los Angeles Lakers Injury Report vs. Blazers Getty Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after making a three-point shot against the Sacramento Kings in the second half of a preseason game at Golden 1 Center on October 05, 2026 in Sacramento, California. The Los Angeles Lakers have four players listed on their injury report against the Portland Trail Blazers. Bronny James and Cameron Carr are both out as they are on assignment with the Coachella Valley Lakers in the NBA G League. It’s a way for James and Carr to get playing time since they aren’t part of JJ Redick ’s current rotation. Getty Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers dribbles upcourt during the second half of a game against the LA Clippers at Intuit Dome on October 28, 2026 in Inglewood, California. Walker Kessler is available to play. He continues to deal with a left finger injury, so he wears a splint. He hasn’t missed a game because of the injury, which means it’s not a big concern for the Lakers. Sandro Mamukelashvili is also on the injury report. He is tagged as questionable because of an illness. He will likely get re-evaluated before tip-off for a final ruling on his status. If Mamukelashvili can’t play, Jarred Vanderbilt and Ziaire Williams could get an uptick in minutes. Adou Thiero to Make Season Debut Getty Adou Thiero #1 of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots the ball against the Sacramento Kings during the first quarter in a preseason game at Crypto.com Arena on October 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. One player off the Lakers injury report is Adou Thiero , who could make his season debut against the Blazers. Thiero missed the first nine games of the season due to inflammation in his surgically repaired left knee. It became swollen in the preseason, so the Lakers managed it to avoid any further complications. The second-year forward missed the majority of his rookie season due to left knee surgery. He might get some playing time if Sandro Mamukelashvili is downgraded to out. Lakers vs. Blazers Preview The Lakers take on the Blazers for the second time this season. They first met at the Moda Center on October 27, with the Blazers earning a 136-129 win. The Lakers were up in the first half, but the Blazers finished the fourth quarter strongly to hand the purple and gold franchise their first defeat of the season. Deni Avdija and Ja Morant each scored 23 points, while Jrue Holiday added 22 points to lead the Blazers. Damian Lillard also scored 21 points as Portland’s team effort prevailed against Luka Doncic ’s 41-point night. Austin Reaves had 26 points for the Lakers, while Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 17 points off the bench. item.title: 'Leaders all over the world understand that Trump is only there for two more years & then he's gone'
item.description: In American politics, even presidential power has its limits. And now, the laws of political gravity may finally be catching up with Donald Trump's hyper-aggressive exercise of executive authority. Following what political scientist Ian Bremmer describes as the most consequential electoral reversal for a governing party in more than half a century, the president and founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media argues that the United States has entered a new political phase: the beginning of the end of Trump's ability to dominate the political agenda, at home and on the world stage.

item.title: Bruins Postgame: Six Goals, What Makes the Team Dangerous
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins keep winning, and the contributions continue to come from all over the ice. The Bruins (12-4-1) exploded for three unanswered goals in their third straight win, beating the Pittsburgh Penguins (5-9-2) 6-2 at PPG Paints Arena on Thursday night. Pavel Zacha scored twice, and Mark Kastelic , Elias Lindholm , Morgan Geekie , and Fraser Minten added one. Michael DiPietro only needed to make 16 saves for the fourth win of his NHL career. Read Next Bruins Rout Penguins, James Hagens Leaves Game Early It is the seventh time this season that five or more Bruins scored in a win. They now have 12 players who have scored three or more goals on the season, with Kastelic joining that group on Thursday. “It’s probably a combo [bringing it together] a little bit,” Marco Sturm said to reporters in Pittsburgh. “I think guys get used to each other, and also just the way we play too. We are deeper this year than in the past, we feel like, and every line can score, and every line can be out there [at] any time of the game. So I think that’s pretty much it.” All four lines factored into the scoring, as well. Marco Sturm has kept the forward lines mostly intact throughout the month of October and into November, and the consistency has paid off. Four of the six goals came from the Bruins’ top two lines, neither of which serves as their shutdown forward line. The fourth line jumped into the fray with a faceoff play that directly set up Kastelic’s goal. Then Elias Lindholm took advantage of a brutal Erik Karlsson defensive-zone turnover to give the Bruins a 3-1 lead in the first period. “I think every line is dangerous out there. I think that it’s been all season,” JJ Peterka said. “That’s why we’re so dangerous (because) it doesn’t really matter who’s out there. Every line can produce offensively, play a good defensive game, and yeah, I think it’s helping us a lot this year.” And yes, the Bruins’ third line, consisting of Casey Mittelstadt , Elias Lindholm, and James Hagens , continued their dominant defensive play. They played together for 8:11 before Hagens left the game early, and in that time, the Penguins generated just 0.03 expected goals compared to the Bruins’ 0.33. The trio also held Sidney Crosby ’s line without a shot on goal in 4:46 of 5-on-5 time against the line. Further, the Bruins held the Penguins’ top line of Crosby, Tommy Novak , and Rickard Rakell without a shot on goal throughout the entire game. “Just with our structure and everything, our ability to kind of not lay low, but I think we rely on our structure a lot throughout the game, and we kind of just wait for mistakes,” Morgan Geekie said about the team’s success. “Teams are good, and sometimes it takes 60 minutes to finally see it break through. The Bruins (12-4-1) exploded for three unanswered goals in their third straight win, beating the Pittsburgh Penguins (5-9-2) 6-2 at PPG Paints Arena on Thursday night. Pavel Zacha scored twice, and Mark Kastelic , Elias Lindholm , Morgan Geekie , and Fraser Minten added one. Michael DiPietro only needed to make 16 saves for the fourth win of his NHL career. Read Next Bruins Rout Penguins, James Hagens Leaves Game Early It is the seventh time this season that five or more Bruins scored in a win. They now have 12 players who have scored three or more goals on the season, with Kastelic joining that group on Thursday. “It’s probably a combo [bringing it together] a little bit,” Marco Sturm said to reporters in Pittsburgh. “I think guys get used to each other, and also just the way we play too. We are deeper this year than in the past, we feel like, and every line can score, and every line can be out there [at] any time of the game. So I think that’s pretty much it.” All four lines factored into the scoring, as well. Marco Sturm has kept the forward lines mostly intact throughout the month of October and into November, and the consistency has paid off. Four of the six goals came from the Bruins’ top two lines, neither of which serves as their shutdown forward line. The fourth line jumped into the fray with a faceoff play that directly set up Kastelic’s goal. Then Elias Lindholm took advantage of a brutal Erik Karlsson defensive-zone turnover to give the Bruins a 3-1 lead in the first period. “I think every line is dangerous out there. I think that it’s been all season,” JJ Peterka said. “That’s why we’re so dangerous (because) it doesn’t really matter who’s out there. Every line can produce offensively, play a good defensive game, and yeah, I think it’s helping us a lot this year.” And yes, the Bruins’ third line, consisting of Casey Mittelstadt , Elias Lindholm, and James Hagens , continued their dominant defensive play. They played together for 8:11 before Hagens left the game early, and in that time, the Penguins generated just 0.03 expected goals compared to the Bruins’ 0.33. The trio also held Sidney Crosby ’s line without a shot on goal in 4:46 of 5-on-5 time against the line. Further, the Bruins held the Penguins’ top line of Crosby, Tommy Novak , and Rickard Rakell without a shot on goal throughout the entire game. “Just with our structure and everything, our ability to kind of not lay low, but I think we rely on our structure a lot throughout the game, and we kind of just wait for mistakes,” Morgan Geekie said about the team’s success. “Teams are good, and sometimes it takes 60 minutes to finally see it break through. Tonight, we saw a couple go in a little earlier than that, but we all kind of play the same way. There’s not really any difference between the four lines. We’re all kind of workers, and I think you kind of just see everybody buy into that program, and you’re seeing everybody get rewarded.” Geekie scored the Bruins’ fifth goal, his third in as many games. He brushed off the previous goal-scoring slump, knowing that the team was winning. On Monday, he joked about catching his brother Conor after scoring his third of the season, and now he has. “No,” Geekie said when asked if scoring three in three lifts his confidence. “It’s always nice, and it’s a privilege to score in this league, and I understand how hard it is. I think when you start to see them go in, you start to get a little nitpicky. I had another chance, almost identical to the one I scored, and that’s going to be the one that’s on my mind, not the one that went in.” “When you win games like we did tonight in the way that we’ve been playing, it makes things a lot easier, and everybody’s happy to come to the rink.” Read Next Bruins’ Morgan Geekie Looks to Regain Scoring Touch The Bruins also got contributions from their blue line. Hampus Lindholm finished with an assist and a plus-4 rating, and Charlie McAvoy finished with a plus-3. In 16:08 together, the Bruins outshot the Penguins 8-4. They outscored them 4-1, and they owned a 70.25% share of expected goals for. Frederic Brunet recorded an assist, setting up Mark Kastelic’s goal in the first period. He missed the previous three games as a healthy scratch, but Sturm was happy with what he saw out of the 23-year-old defenseman in his first game back. “Yeah, it was a great shot,” Sturm said. “He’s done it in the past with that sneaky shot, but he was good. He was fine. He was absolutely fine. I’m happy.” The Bruins still sit at the top of the Atlantic Division and have done so since October 16. They have won three in a row for the second time this season, and they sit three points behind the Carolina Hurricanes (13-3-2) at the top of the Eastern Conference. The Bruins now return home, where they are 7-1-0 this season, for their second divisional matchup of the season. They will play the Florida Panthers at 1:00 PM on Sunday in their second of nine home games in November. The Bruins dropped their only Atlantic Division matchup this season, and Florida is also searching for their first win in the division. item.title: Syracuse’s Gerry McNamara Peels Back Curtain On Gavin Doty, Mark Morano
item.description: GREENVILLE, SOUTH CAROLINA - MARCH 18: Gavin Doty #4 of the Siena Saints speaks with the media during practice day ahead of the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Bon Secours Wellness Arena on March 18, 2026 in Greenville, South Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Syracuse Orange didn’t please new head coach Gerry McNamara with their season-opening win over New Haven earlier this week. G-Mac was happier after their Thursday night win over Central Connecticut State. McNamara is always going to find moments where SU can improve, but he felt Syracuse was closer to its best self on Thursday. The score certainly looks a lot better — Syracuse won 102-49. It was a balanced effort from the Orange, too. Gavin Doty led the way with 18 points. Mark Morano had 16 points. Luke Wilson had 14 points from his center position. Sadiq White put up 8 points with 10 rebounds. and Garwey Dual rounded out the starters with 8 points and 4 assists. Off the bench, Kiyan Anthony dropped 14 points for the Orange. Amarri Monroe and Tasman Goodrick each added 8 points off the bench themselves. Most notable after the game was the way McNamara talked about Doty and Morano. Gerry McNamara on Gavin Doty McNamara was asked “what it takes to get Gavin Doty’s motor going” in his postgame press conference. G-Mac laughed. “What does it take to get Gavin Doty’s motor going?” McNamara laughed. “Nothing. Nothing. He’s going to figure it out. I don’t have to do anything to get his motor going. He’s gonna play hard every second, every possession. He’s gonna find a way. There’s no telling Gav he’s not playing hard enough. There’s coaching him on certain things in terms of over-aggression sometimes. He’s gonna find something.” Doty came with McNamara from Siena, and it wasn’t immediately clear how he might translate. And sure, this isn’t ACC play at the moment. But right now, Doty looks like he belongs, and his motor helps that cause. Gerry McNamara on Mark Morano Morano hit three 3-pointers in the opener and hit four 3-pointers on Thursday night. That’s going to be his role in the Syracuse starting lineup, to be sure. “We ran a play for him and he didn’t shoot it, so I screamed at him,” McNamara said. “He’s a good player. Right at the start of the game he got downhill and made a layup. It’s undeniable he’s a really good offensive player. He can find the net. He’s bigger than you think. He’s a legit 6-6. The kid’s got big-time potential… He shoots the blood out of the ball, and I need him to shoot it when he’s open.” Morano came to Syracuse as a highly touted recruit from Slovenia. This is his first college basketball experience, and he’s off to a great start. It was a balanced effort from the Orange, too. Gavin Doty led the way with 18 points. Mark Morano had 16 points. Luke Wilson had 14 points from his center position. Sadiq White put up 8 points with 10 rebounds. and Garwey Dual rounded out the starters with 8 points and 4 assists. Off the bench, Kiyan Anthony dropped 14 points for the Orange. Amarri Monroe and Tasman Goodrick each added 8 points off the bench themselves. Most notable after the game was the way McNamara talked about Doty and Morano. Gerry McNamara on Gavin Doty McNamara was asked “what it takes to get Gavin Doty’s motor going” in his postgame press conference. G-Mac laughed. “What does it take to get Gavin Doty’s motor going?” McNamara laughed. “Nothing. Nothing. He’s going to figure it out. I don’t have to do anything to get his motor going. He’s gonna play hard every second, every possession. He’s gonna find a way. There’s no telling Gav he’s not playing hard enough. There’s coaching him on certain things in terms of over-aggression sometimes. He’s gonna find something.” Doty came with McNamara from Siena, and it wasn’t immediately clear how he might translate. And sure, this isn’t ACC play at the moment. But right now, Doty looks like he belongs, and his motor helps that cause. Gerry McNamara on Mark Morano Morano hit three 3-pointers in the opener and hit four 3-pointers on Thursday night. That’s going to be his role in the Syracuse starting lineup, to be sure. “We ran a play for him and he didn’t shoot it, so I screamed at him,” McNamara said. “He’s a good player. Right at the start of the game he got downhill and made a layup. It’s undeniable he’s a really good offensive player. He can find the net. He’s bigger than you think. He’s a legit 6-6. The kid’s got big-time potential… He shoots the blood out of the ball, and I need him to shoot it when he’s open.” Morano came to Syracuse as a highly touted recruit from Slovenia. This is his first college basketball experience, and he’s off to a great start. item.title: ‘You Can’t Run Your Mouth All Week,’ ‘Talking All This Fake Tough Stuff’ — Shannon Sharpe Rips Jared Verse After Browns Star Calls Out Teammates
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse (8) walks off the field during the fourth quarter of an NFL game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. © Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse criticized his teammates for not standing up for him after Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick took him down during a point-after attempt in their Week 8 game. Verse had made fiery comments about the Steelers before the matchup, but none of his teammates came to his defense when McCormick, who was penalized, swept his legs and sent him falling awkwardly. NFL icon Shannon Sharpe also weighed in on Verse’s comments, adding to the debate among fans and analysts. Shannon Sharpe Rips Jared Verse for Calling Out His Teammates While speaking to reporters on Thursday, Verse did not mince his words about how he felt when his teammates did not back him up in a tense AFC North game in Pittsburgh. The two-time Pro Bowler admitted he did not let his teammates know he would trash-talk the Steelers, including saying the Browns intended to “make Pittsburgh ours.” “The lack of reaction by those around me upset me a lot,” Verse admitted. “A similar play happened to Derek Barnett, I think, on the next field goal, and I lost it because it was my brothers and my teammates. And when you do something like that to him, it upsets me very deeply,” he said. During Thursday’s segment of the “Nightcap” podcast, Sharpe was adamant that Verse’s off-field actions towards his teammates contributed to their reaction when he was body-slammed in Pittsburgh. “I know this ain’t the guy talking about he mad at his teammates,” Sharpe said . “I know this ain’t the same guy that didn’t show up to Deshaun Watson’s victory party that he had at his house because he said it was an hour away. That ain’t that Jared Verse. Oh, we a team. But when a teammate has a get-together, ‘I ain’t driving no hour.’ Really? Guess what, when you run your mouth, and a dude power bombs you, that ain’t got nothing to do with me.” “You out here running your mouth, talking all this fake tough stuff before the game, and then when Mason McCormick body-slams you on your head, nobody moves. Not one of your teammates stepped up.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “Not one person came over to back you up. You can’t go around picking fights. Guys in a group will pick a fight, but when they’re by themselves, they’re quieter than church mice. You ain’t got your group with you. Run your mouth now,” he added. “In the NFL, if you’re gonna talk like a big dawg, you’d better play like a big dawg. You can’t run your mouth all week and then get handled like that without your own team having your back,” Sharpe concluded. Verse was traded to the Browns as part of the blockbuster deal that saw two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett move to the Rams earlier this year. The Rams selected Verse No. 19 overall in the 202

item.title: Allan Saint-Maximin explains why Steve Bruce is the greatest manager he has ever played under
item.description: Allan Saint-Maximin and Steve Bruce Allan Saint-Maximin has been talking about the managers he has played under, including at Newcastle United. United one of the eleven clubs he has played for in his career, so far. The enigmatic winger spent four seasons at St James’ Park, the longest he has ever been at a club. His 11th and latest club is Charlotte FC who are currently fifth in the MLS Eastern Conference 2026 table after 33 matches. Allan Saint-Maximin joined them in their mid-season transfer window in July, he has scored twice and got four assists in 14 matches for the team managed by Dean Smith (formerly Aston Villa manager), who have qualified for the MLS play-offs. They have one match of the normal league season still to go but last weekend Allan Saint-Maximin was sent off at the end of Charlotte’s 4-0 victory over Orlando for grabbing his crotch in the direction of an opponent. The former Newcastle United winger spent the second half of the 2025/26 season with Lens, they were desperate to keep Allan Saint-Maximim after he helped them win the French Cup and finish runners-up in Ligue 1. ASM scoring four goals and providing three assists in 13 appearances. However, the French winger opting to move to yet another new club for a new adventure with Charlotte FC. In an interview with The Athletic , Allan Saint-Maximin saying he had offers to leave Newcastle United but turned them down because he believed he owed NUFC commitment: “They gave me everything. It’s like with your kids. You prepare everything for them. You take the poo, you clean, you do every single thing you can. And when they get to the top, they look at you like, ‘Thanks, Dad, now you can go away, I will live my life’. No, you cannot betray like this. They gave me everything and it was very important to be loyal.” Allan Saint-Maximin says he enjoyed playing under Eddie Howe at Newcastle United: “So many good players came, so we started to play better, that’s why we reached the Champions League.” However, ASM naming the best ever manager he has played under across his entire career. Allan Saint-Maximin naming Steve Bruce as his favourite manager across his whole career, as he gave him the trust and freedom to express himself: “Incredible manager but we didn’t have an unbelievable squad.” Allan Saint-Maximin though naming the Newcastle United fans as his absolute favourite, giving him his greatest memories: “I will never, ever forget them.” Allan Saint-Maximin picks the 3-3 draw with Manchester City on 21 August 2022 as his top standout NUFC match memory: “When you play against the top team, you see Guardiola down the line and you get the ball and he puts his hand on his head to be like, ‘What is this player? He’s a nightmare’. You feel something’s different. To feel the voice of the crowd when you get the ball, you feel them pushing you, you feel like you are flying. It’s something special.” The Athletic also reporting: Another notable moment was his winning goal against Oxford Unit

As Saint-Maximin celebrated during the match shown live on BBC One, a Newcastle supporter was seen exposing himself in the away end. Those are the things that help you understand Newcastle.” In a previous interview in September with BBC Sport , Allan Saint-Maximin said that he hoped Matthias Jaissle and his backroom staff would “have the best possible time” with Newcastle United, just as he did. Matthias Jaissle was appointed by Al-Ahli on 29 July 2023, only 24 hours after ASM had signed for them. The newly promoted club then saw the new manager and winger help guide them to third place in the Saudi Pro league, in the only season Matthias Jaissle and Allan Saint-Maximin spent together.

item.title: Giants DC Dennard Wilson drops defiant truth bomb on holding his defense accountable
item.description: Denny Simmons / The Tennessean / USA TODAY NETWORK Giants DC Dennard Wilson drops defiant truth bomb on holding his defense accountable appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dennard Wilson has not been shy about calling out the New York Giants ’ defense this season, and the defensive coordinator is not changing his approach as the team prepares to face the Philadelphia Eagles. Asked whether there is a danger in being so blunt publicly, Wilson did not flinch . “I think we get too caught up into not speaking the truth, right? The film doesn’t lie, and it never lies. And it’s always evidence. It’s a solid tape. And what I said in front of this podium, they’ve heard me say it from the first day they were here. So it’s nothing that they haven’t heard before,” Wilson said, via SNY. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Dennard Wilson talks about holding himself and his defense accountable: "We get too caught up in not speaking the truth. The film doesn't lie…too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations" pic.twitter.com/5OOKpo14dQ — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) November 5, 2026 “It’s not calling out a specific player. It’s calling out a behavior. It’s calling out what we’re not doing collectively, because at the end of the day, it’s me as well. So if I let it slip, shame on me,” he continued. “You know, I think too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations.” Wilson added that a strong bond with his players is what allows him to be so direct. “If you build a relationship and you have this bond and you have this tight-knit group, you can speak to them in a certain way and identify certain things without attacking them personally. It’s not a personal attack. It’s a behavioral attack,” Wilson said. “And that’s how I go about it, and that’s how I’ve been trained to do this since I was a young coach 20-some years ago.” Wilson made headlines last month after a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints, when the Giants missed 18 tackles. He did not hold back, labeling players who do not run to the ball as “traitors to the defense” and warning that “if you don’t change the behaviors, we have to change the players.” New York bounced back with a 27-21 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 7, and the Giants enter Sunday’s matchup at 4-2-1 coming off their bye. Wilson joined John Harbaugh’s staff in January after two seasons as the Tennessee Titans’ defensive coordinator, reuniting with the coach he worked under in Baltimore. The Giants will now look to keep it rolling against an Eagles team that has dropped six straight games. Related: Giants WR Malik Nabers eases injury concerns with 3-word declaration Related: Giants’ Isaiah Likely drops ‘more the merrier’ admission on New York’s potential trades

item.title: Patrick Ngongba Sets Career High In Duke Win
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 20: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts following a basket during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Volunteers at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 20, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils dunks the ball during the first half of the game against the Army Black Knights at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) Getty DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils jostles with Tate Laczkowski #32 and Jacen Holloway #10 of the Army Black Knights for a rebound during the second half of the game at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) Getty WASHINGTON, DC - MARCH 27: Patrick Ngongba #21 and Caleb Foster #1 of the Duke Blue Devils celebrate during the second half against the St. John's Red Storm in the Sweet Sixteen of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Capital One Arena on March 27, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Patrick Ngongba scored a career-high 28 points in Duke’s 113-52 win over Coastal Carolina. Throughout the game, Ngongba dominated in the paint. He used his height and size to take advantage of the smaller Coastal Carolina team. He overwhelmed them and proved to be too much for them. Patrick Ngongba: His Impressive Performance Getty DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA – NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils dunks the ball during the first half of the game against the Army Black Knights at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) Ngongba entered halftime with 18 points; he set the tone early on and continued throughout the whole half. He ended up scoring 10 more points in the second half, giving him his career high of 28 points. He was 10/13 from the field and 6/10 from the free-throw line. He even showcased his outside shooting, going 2/3 from three-point range. He spent the whole first half around the rim, catching alley-oops and backing the opponent down. It was important for him to establish the paint game early on to dictate how the game was going to go. That put a lot of pressure on Coastal Carolina to figure out how to stop it. He was able to draw a bunch of fouls, adding even more pressure to their team. In the second half, he hit back-to-back three-pointers, showing that he is more than a paint scorer. More Than Scoring Getty DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA – NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils jostles with Tate Laczkowski #32 and Jacen Holloway #10 of the Army Black Knights for a rebound during the second half of the game at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) Ng

Patrick Ngongba: His Impressive Performance Getty DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA – NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils dunks the ball during the first half of the game against the Army Black Knights at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) Ngongba entered halftime with 18 points; he set the tone early on and continued throughout the whole half. He ended up scoring 10 more points in the second half, giving him his career high of 28 points. He was 10/13 from the field and 6/10 from the free-throw line. He even showcased his outside shooting, going 2/3 from three-point range. He spent the whole first half around the rim, catching alley-oops and backing the opponent down. It was important for him to establish the paint game early on to dictate how the game was going to go. That put a lot of pressure on Coastal Carolina to figure out how to stop it. More Than Scoring Getty DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA – NOVEMBER 02: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils jostles with Tate Laczkowski #32 and Jacen Holloway #10 of the Army Black Knights for a rebound during the second half of the game at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 02, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Alex Halloway/Getty Images) Ngongba also had nine rebounds and a block, giving Duke a defensive presence. He didn’t have a lot of blocks, but he forced misses from all over the court. His defense may have even been more important than his offense. He has become more versatile on both ends through his time at Duke so far. Ngongba makes players change their shots at times and creates difficult shots. His ability to make a difference on both ends is way more valuable than just his scoring. He plays hard every play and never takes a play off. How He Complements the Guards Getty WASHINGTON, DC – MARCH 27: Patrick Ngongba #21 and Caleb Foster #1 of the Duke Blue Devils celebrate during the second half against the St. John’s Red Storm in the Sweet Sixteen of the 2026 NCAA Men’s Basketball Tournament at Capital One Arena on March 27, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Ngongba is the perfect match for the guards that the Blue Devils have. Defensively, the guards like to pressure everyone up the court, so if they get beat, Ngongba is there to block a shot or force a turnover. He gives the guards the capability to pressure without worrying if they are going to get beat. Opposing teams don’t want to drive it in on Ngongba. Offensively, Cayden Boozer, Dame Sarr, Caleb Foster, and Deron Rippey Jr. like to attack the paint. This draws the bugs to try to block their shots, which leaves Ngongba wide open for a lob. He is also a really good passer, so when he gets double-teamed in the paint, he will kick it out to whichever guard is open. They all work well together. This is a good game for Ngongba to build on going forward. Establishing dominance in the paint will open up so much more for the rest of the Duke team. He draws so much attention and commands a double team. This was a great game for him and a confidence booster heading into a juggernaut of a schedule. item.title: Will It Rain at Interlagos? Sao Paulo GP Weather Forecast Puts Qualifying Most at Risk
item.description: Weather forecast for the 2026 Sao Paulo GP says Saturday's qualifying could be affected by heavy rain. (Source: MEGA) Saturday is the day to watch the sky at Interlagos. Formula 1's official forecast for the Sao Paulo GP gives a 50% chance of rain on Saturday, November 7, most likely after 2 PM and possibly lasting into the evening. That window lands right on top of qualifying, which starts at 3 PM local time, so the session that sets Sunday's grid carries the biggest risk of the weekend. The warning is substantial. The official forecast says that "if rain does occur, it could be significant," and it adds that some streets in the city could flood and standing water could form on the track. Even without a storm, gusts could reach 50 km/h (31 mph), and strong winds will affect drivers in the braking zones. F1 WARNS OF POSSIBLE FLOODING AT INTERLAGOS Formula 1's official São Paulo GP weather forecast highlights a significant risk of rain this weekend: Friday: 30% Saturday: 50% Sunday: 40% Saturday is the biggest concern, with heavy rain possible after 2 PM local… pic.twitter.com/tyajxgaycu — Everything Formula (@evrythngformu1a) November 5, 2026 Sunday doesn't look much different either. Race day should be cool and possibly unsettled, with temperatures between 13 C and 19 C (55 F to 66 F) and a 40% chance of heavy rain and thunderstorms. Still, the timing of Saturday's threat makes qualifying the session most likely to turn out chaotic. Max Verstappen didn't hide his excitement at Thursday's press conference. The Red Bull driver, who won from 17th at Interlagos in 2024, recalled "crazy races" there, including wins from the front and from the back in the rain. "It's looking like there's a chance of rain again, so that's exciting," he said. Why Saturday Afternoon Is the Danger Zone at Sao Paulo GP Interlagos makes its own weather, and the Audi F1 team explained how this week. Two reservoirs sit on either side of the circuit and put a lot of moisture into the air, and sudden temperature shifts can help storms form. Audi has explained why the Sao Paulo GP is always at risk of being affected by rain and storms. (Source: MEGA) The track also sits on a hillside about 800 meters above sea level, which pushes damp air upward, where it cools and falls as rain. That's not just a theory. Audi pointed out that wet weather has been a major factor in qualifying here in three of the last four seasons. In 2024, a heavy storm pushed qualifying back to Sunday morning, and a year later the FIA issued a rare level 4 rain warning for Saturday. Last year's Sao Paulo GP, though, ran in dry conditions, with Lando Norris winning for McLaren ahead of Antonelli and Verstappen. However, this year could be a different story. PlanetF1 , writing on November 4, put the risk at 60% for final practice and 30% for qualifying, with Sunday's race facing a 50-60% chance. Max Verstappen's epic storm lap Brazil 2023 pic.twitter.com/OE7ZY7ZH3A — MV33Racing (@MV33Racing) November 3, 2026 Fri
item.content:encoded: Weather forecast for the 2026 Sao Paulo GP says Saturday's qualifying could be affected by heavy rain. (Source: MEGA) Saturday is the day to watch the sky at Interlagos. Formula 1's official forecast for the Sao Paulo GP gives a 50% chance of rain on Saturday, November 7, most likely after 2 PM and possibly lasting into the evening. That window lands right on top of qualifying, which starts at 3 PM local time, so the session that sets Sunday's grid carries the biggest risk of the weekend. The warning is substantial. The official forecast says that "if rain does occur, it could be significant," and it adds that some streets in the city could flood and standing water could form on the track. Even without a storm, gusts could reach 50 km/h (31 mph), and strong winds will affect drivers in the braking zones. F1 WARNS OF POSSIBLE FLOODING AT INTERLAGOS Formula 1's official São Paulo GP weather forecast highlights a significant risk of rain this weekend: Friday: 30% Saturday: 50% Sunday: 40% Saturday is the biggest concern, with heavy rain possible after 2 PM local… pic.twitter.com/tyajxgaycu — Everything Formula (@evrythngformu1a) November 5, 2026 Sunday doesn't look much different either. Race day should be cool and possibly unsettled, with temperatures between 13 C and 19 C (55 F to 66 F) and a 40% chance of heavy rain and thunderstorms. Still, the timing of Saturday's threat makes qualifying the session most likely to turn out chaotic. Max Verstappen didn't hide his excitement at Thursday's press conference. The Red Bull driver, who won from 17th at Interlagos in 2024, recalled "crazy races" there, including wins from the front and from the back in the rain. "It's looking like there's a chance of rain again, so that's exciting," he said. Why Saturday Afternoon Is the Danger Zone at Sao Paulo GP Interlagos makes its own weather, and the Audi F1 team explained how this week. Two reservoirs sit on either side of the circuit and put a lot of moisture into the air, and sudden temperature shifts can help storms form. Audi has explained why the Sao Paulo GP is always at risk of being affected by rain and storms. (Source: MEGA) The track also sits on a hillside about 800 meters above sea level, which pushes damp air upward, where it cools and falls as rain. That's not just a theory. Audi pointed out that wet weather has been a major factor in qualifying here in three of the last four seasons. In 2024, a heavy storm pushed qualifying back to Sunday morning, and a year later the FIA issued a rare level 4 rain warning for Saturday. Last year's Sao Paulo GP, though, ran in dry conditions, with Lando Norris winning for McLaren ahead of Antonelli and Verstappen. However, this year could be a different story. PlanetF1 , writing on November 4, put the risk at 60% for final practice and 30% for qualifying, with Sunday's race facing a 50-60% chance. Max Verstappen's epic storm lap Brazil 2023 pic.twitter.com/OE7ZY7ZH3A — MV33Racing (@MV33Racing) November 3, 2026 Friday’s practice is expected to give teams a dry track. The official forecast calls for mostly cloudy, dry conditions, with a 30% chance of rain mainly in the early morning and at night. Williams warned that the weather could leave teams with little representative dry running before qualifying and the race, which makes Friday's laps worth more than usual. There's no sprint this year either, so teams get a third practice session at 11:30 AM Saturday. Verstappen said the extra setup time "might be good or might be bad." If you only watch one session live this weekend, make it qualifying. Drivers Joke, but Malaysia's Wet-Weather Glitch Still Lingers The rain talk on Thursday quickly turned to software. Bruna Parreira of Globo TV asked the drivers whether they worried that the 2026 cars might run into more problems in the wet, after software issues in the rain in Malaysia. Verstappen didn't miss a beat: "I installed antivirus on my car, so I'll be fine." Max Verstappen kept the mood light over the potential software issues in wet Sao Paulo GP conditions. (Source: MEGA) He then teased Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad , reminding him that both teams use the same power unit. The laughs covered a real problem from earlier this season. During the wet race in Malaysia, a power unit software bug appeared, and the race got underway only after the FIA sent teams new software about 20 minutes later. Nikolas Tombazis , the FIA's single-seater director, said he could guarantee that this specific bug wouldn't return but couldn't rule out every bug. He'd already admitted that the FIA hadn't been able to test the 2026 cars enough in wet conditions beforehand. Fernando Alonso pictured exactly where a glitch would hurt most. "Hopefully not, because that is quite steep uphill, you know, after the last corner," said the two-time champion, who added that he believes the problems were understood after Malaysia. Fernando Alonso hopes the software glitch from Malaysia doesn’t affect the cars in the Sao Paulo GP. (Source: MEGA) Not everyone sees the clouds as bad news. Alpine's Franco Colapinto said Brazil's rain always brings new chances for his team, and home hero Gabriel Bortoleto said the weather can be crazy and anything can happen at Interlagos. Mercedes may need some luck, too, since the team must beat Ferrari by three points this weekend to seal the Constructors' title. Antonelli arrives with nothing left to prove and nothing left to protect. Verstappen arrives as the man who loves this place most when it's wet. Somewhere over the lakes, a storm may be deciding who starts where.

item.title: Warriors predicted to trade Kristaps Porzingis for $27M versatile stretch-big after recent update
item.description: Warriors predicted to trade Kristaps Porzingis for $27M versatile stretch-big after recent update originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors have an interesting situation on their hands that has nothing to do with basketball and everything to do with a health issue that has created plenty of uncertainty. Kristaps Porzingis still hasn’t returned to the team after being diagnosed with POTS. The veteran center became aware of the condition shortly after training camp began. Now, Golden State is reportedly exploring ways to move his contract through a trade. “Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN," ESPN's Shams Charania posted. The Warriors are certainly in a position they didn't expect to be in this early in the season. The team has been rolling, but missing a big man is never easy under any circumstances. The Athletic’s Nick Friedell reported Wednesday that the organization doesn't expect Porzingis to return to the floor. “Warriors players/coaches seem to have moved on from the idea that Porzingis will be back with the team. They are hopeful that he can get healthy, but aren't expecting him back on the floor,” Friedell wrote. With Golden State exploring trade options, Sports Illustrated’s Joey Akeley believes a deal for Chicago Bulls forward Jalen Smith could be in play. The proposed trade would send Smith and a second-round pick to the Warriors in exchange for Porzingis and a first-round pick. “Warriors get: Jalen Smith, 2027 second-round pick (via Cleveland). Bulls get: Kristaps Porzingis, 2027 first-round pick (top-11-protected),” Akeley wrote. This deal could benefit the Warriors by bringing in a versatile frontcourt player while moving Porzingis' contract. Smith can fill multiple roles and give Golden State another inside presence when needed. Smith is playing under a contract worth approximately $27 million over its full term. He is a well-rounded player who could make an impact for the Warriors this season. More MLB news: Lakers predicted to trade for $88M rim-runner to reunite with Luka Doncic amid lethal start 76ers' Tyrese Maxey gives great injury update on pinky finger after revenge win vs. Pistons Warriors' Kristaps Porzingis future appears headed toward one brutal ending amid ongoing saga Warriors predicted to trade Draymond Green for $186M rebounding savant for Steph Curry Finals run

item.title: 2027: INEC chairman seeks traditional rulers’ support for credible polls
item.description: ….Commissions BVAS storage centre in Kogi By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, has sought the support of traditional rulers in Kogi State for the conduct of peaceful, transparent and credible elections ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan made the appeal on Thursday in Lokoja during an engagement with traditional rulers from the 21 local government areas of the state. The INEC chairman said he visited the state alongside his team to assess the preparedness of the commission’s personnel and infrastructure ahead of the 2027 general elections and the forthcoming off-cycle governorship election. He said the commission was committed to strengthening its operational capacity through infrastructure upgrades and the deployment of modern technological tools to ensure seamless electoral processes. Amupitan urged traditional rulers to use their influence and close relationship with grassroots communities to promote peaceful conduct, voter awareness and acceptance of credible electoral outcomes. Speaking at the engagement, the Kogi State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Prof. Shehu Wahab, commended the traditional rulers for their sustained cooperation with the commission. Wahab said the support of traditional institutions remained vital to successful electoral activities, particularly in promoting peace and encouraging citizens to participate actively in the democratic process. Responding, the traditional rulers pledged to communicate the INEC chairman’s message to their subjects and assured the commission of their commitment to peaceful, transparent and credible elections in the state. Earlier, Amupitan commissioned the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) storage centre at the INEC state headquarters in Lokoja as part of efforts to strengthen the commission’s operational infrastructure ahead of future elections. The post 2027: INEC chairman seeks traditional rulers’ support for credible polls appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Hospital gave very sick doctor a special PC for his personal, erm, pleasure
item.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to a fresh edition of On Call, The Register 's weekly tale of tech support trials and tribulations that readers kindly share. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Mason," who told us he once worked at a hospital doing tech support for its research labs. "One of the labs was for a doctor who was one of the world's top organ transplant researchers" Mason told On Call. The doctor was also a voracious consumer of – ahem – adult entertainment, a habit that saw his PC and other machines around the lab often come down with a nasty case of malware. Mason got to clean that up, sometimes multiple times in a single week. The doctor's foibles were widely known around the hospital, as was the fact that his activities violated several workplace policies. Mason pointed this out to his boss every time he cleaned up a fresh malware outbreak but such was the doctor's status that management never intervened. And then the hospital was hit by a nasty cyber-worm that did a lot of damage. During the cleanup, Mason's colleagues found logs that showed the doctor's PC was the source of the infection, and that he had been indulging in his online hobby at the time the worm arrived. Mason assumed this would be the moment at which the doctor would finally be held accountable and face disciplinary action. Instead the doctor made a bargain with the IT department to henceforth use only a designated PC when pursuing – ahem – personal and/or intimate matters. And he would only use office PCs for actual work. The hospital's tech team rescued a PC from its e-waste pile for this job. "Get this thing going and deliver it to Doctor Pervert," Mason's boss ordered. By this stage, Mason had had enough. He escalated his protests, telling his boss that indulging this doctor was unprofessional, likely exposed the hospital to lawsuits, wasted IT department resources, and was just wrong. "What do you want to hear?" his boss replied. "The CIO told me do this or get another job." After Mason prepped that PC, he only needed to clean up malware about once a year – after the poor machine was so overrun with malware that it no longer served the doctor's purposes. Mason left the hospital while this PC was still in place. "You'll be shocked, no doubt, to learn that years later the doctor's graduate students filed a lawsuit," he told On Call. "And that the separate fun-time computer was one of the pieces of evidence that the hospital knew about his – ahem – proclivities and not just ignored them but facilitated them." Have you been asked to cover up revolting behavior? Or ignore policy? Click here to share your story with On Call. It's our policy to tell a great tech support story week, so we appreciate every contribution. ®

item.title: FCCPC seals firms as oil, salt samples fail fortification tests
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has sealed manufacturing facilities of defaulting food companies after laboratory tests revealed that 12 per cent of vegetable oil and two per cent of salt samples sold in Nigerian markets failed to meet mandatory micronutrient fortification standards. Executive Vice Chairman of FCCPC, Tunji Bello, disclosed this yesterday while presenting findings from a two-month market survey conducted in partnership with the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN), which exposed gaps in compliance with Nigeria’s food fortification policy, raising concerns over consumers’ access to essential nutrients through everyday food products. The survey examined 200 randomly selected samples, comprising 100 vegetable oil and 100 salt products collected from households and open markets across Northern and Southern Nigeria. Laboratory analysis revealed that 12 per cent of vegetable oil samples and two per cent of salt samples were inadequately fortified with essential micronutrients at household level. Of the 100 vegetable oil samples, 49 were unbranded, while 51 were branded products. The investigation also uncovered poor adoption of digital traceability systems for monitoring fortified food products along the supply chain. Only six vegetable oil manufacturers had registered on GAIN’s Digital Fortification Quality Traceability Plus platform, while three companies uploaded a combined eight product test results. Bello said large-scale food fortification was a mandatory public health policy aimed at tackling micronutrient deficiencies through the addition of essential nutrients, including vitamin A, iron, folic acid, zinc and iodine. He stated: “Consumers must be able to trust the quality of the products they buy and the health benefits those products are advertised to provide. “Consumer protection goes beyond resolving everyday complaints or halting deceptive business practices. It fundamentally comes down to ensuring that citizens are not denied the essential value, safety and nutritional benefits they pay for in the marketplace.” He said compliance directives had been issued to defaulting manufacturers, stressing that every batch of food products must meet established quality and safety standards. Bello added that the survey findings had been forwarded to the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) for further regulatory action under the existing memorandum of understanding between both agencies. The post FCCPC seals firms as oil, salt samples fail fortification tests appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump blames Democrats’ midterm wins for US stock market plunge
item.description: US President Donald Trump has blamed the stock market’s sharp decline on the electoral victories recorded by the opposition Democratic Party in the midterm elections earlier this week. Trump made the accusation on Thursday in a post on his Truth Social platform, following a sharp selloff in US equities. “The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame!” he wrote. However, market analysts attributed the selloff largely to concerns that Democratic electoral gains could threaten investments in artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, amid growing opposition to such projects across the United States. The technology-focused Nasdaq recorded its worst percentage decline in a single session since April 2025. Data centre projects have faced opposition from voters across party lines, with several candidates who won seats in the midterm elections pledging to restrict or slow down their development. The Democrats made significant gains, flipping seats previously held by Republicans in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins, securing the party’s seventh Senate seat captured from Republicans. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the traditionally conservative state since 1932, while Iowa elected a Democratic senator for the first time since 2008. In Texas, Democrat Talarico declared that he had defeated “Goliath” after winning a Senate seat, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the governorship. Democrats also retained key Senate seats, including that of Jon Ossoff in Georgia, as well as an open seat in New Hampshire. Their gains extended to Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. In the House of Representatives, Democrats recorded gains across Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had won comfortably in 2024. In one closely watched contest in Indiana, Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican Congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump had carried by 17 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. The Democrats also won Georgia’s governorship, with former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms making history as the state’s first Black woman governor. Republicans, however, secured victories in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state’s first Black governor, while Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat after overcoming a strong Democratic challenge. AFP The post Trump blames Democrats’ midterm wins for US stock market plunge appeared first on Vanguard News .

In Texas, Democrat Talarico declared that he had defeated “Goliath” after winning a Senate seat, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the governorship. Democrats also retained key Senate seats, including that of Jon Ossoff in Georgia, as well as an open seat in New Hampshire. Their gains extended to Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. In the House of Representatives, Democrats recorded gains across Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had won comfortably in 2024. In one closely watched contest in Indiana, Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican Congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump had carried by 17 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. The Democrats also won Georgia’s governorship, with former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms making history as the state’s first Black woman governor. Republicans, however, secured victories in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds became the state’s first Black governor, while Ashley Moody retained a Senate seat after overcoming a strong Democratic challenge. item.title: Power supply plunges as gas shortage, water level worsen
item.description: By Udeme Akpan, Obas Esiedesa & Ediri Ejor There are indications that electricity supply to consumers nationwide has worsened, with Distribution Companies (DisCos) receiving 2,926 megawatts (MW), amid inadequate gas supply, reduced water inflows into hydroelectric reservoirs and other operational constraints. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed a distribution across the DisCos with Abuja, Benin, Eko, Enugu and Ibadan DisCos receiving 633MW, 264MW, 256MW, 253MW and 391MW, respectively. Similarly, Ikeja, Jos, Kaduna, Kano, Port Harcourt and Yola DisCos received 249MW, 146MW, 167MW, 173MW, 320MW and 74MW, respectively. Explaining the decline, NISO stated: “The limited availability of gas has constrained the capacity of affected thermal generating stations to operate at their available levels, while reduced water inflows into reservoirs have impacted the generation capacity of hydroelectric power stations.” The operator added that the constraints had reduced electricity allocations to DisCos, resulting in fewer hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. “Consequently, the reduction in available generation has affected the quantum of electricity allocated to Distribution Companies (DisCos) for onward supply to consumers, thereby resulting in reduced hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks,” it stated further. Similarly, the Federal Ministry of Power acknowledged the impact of the outages on households, businesses and public institutions, particularly in areas that had recently recorded improvements in electricity supply. A statement signed by Adeola Adelabu, Special Adviser (Media and Publicity) to the Minister of Power, the ministry said: “We recognise what every hour without power means for individuals, families and businesses, and we do not take it lightly.” The Ministry further said preliminary assessments showed that the disruptions were not caused by any major or systemic failure of the national grid. It explained: “They stem from maintenance and operational issues on parts of the power ecosystem, together with a decline in generation caused by constraints in gas supply to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower water inflows into reservoirs.” The ministry disclosed that the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, was working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), NISO and DisCos to resolve the operational constraints, accelerate ongoing maintenance and restore normal supply. Meanwhile, generation had recovered to 3,688.95MW as of the time of filing this report, indicating a possible improvement in electricity supply. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 6, 2026
item.description: The US dollar is trading at about ₦1,400 on the parallel market on Friday, November 6, 2026, while the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) rate stood at approximately ₦1,348.74 per dollar at the close of the previous trading session. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the naira exchanged at ₦1,348.74 per dollar on Thursday, November 5, representing a slight depreciation from the previous session’s rate. The NFEM rate is calculated using the volume-weighted average of transactions and serves as Nigeria’s official exchange rate benchmark. Meanwhile, in the parallel market, commonly known as the black market, the dollar was quoted at approximately ₦1,400 on Friday. However, actual buying and selling rates may differ depending on the location, dealer and availability of foreign exchange. The difference between the official and parallel market rates reflects continued demand for foreign currencies outside the formal banking system. Nigerians, particularly importers, businesses, students abroad and individuals making international payments, continue to monitor movements in both markets. The exchange rates may change during the day as trading activities and demand for foreign currencies evolve. The post Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 6, 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu has shown he cares about workers with ₦70,000 allowance — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, insisting that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. Oshiomhole also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which Atiku Abubakar served as vice-president, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. He said the 2027 presidential election would offer Nigerians a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whom he accused of allowing multiple exchange rates that favoured people based on their connections. The senator also faulted the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, for allegedly failing to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” Oshiomhole said. While acknowledging the right of opposition candidates to contest the presidency, he argued that Tinubu should be allowed to continue in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” The post Tinubu has shown he cares about workers with ₦70,000 allowance — Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: IPOB demands release of detained Igbo men, alleges persecution
item.description: ….Group says release of four men after four years in DSS custody exposes alleged injustice By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has demanded the release of Igbo people it claims are being unlawfully detained across correctional facilities in the country, alleging continued persecution of Ndigbo. The group said the recent court-ordered release of four Igbo men, who were reportedly held in the custody of the Department of State Services (DSS) for almost four years, exposed what it described as systemic injustice against the people. IPOB, in a statement by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, titled, “The Persecution of Biafrans Must End: A Demand for Accountability and Rule of Law,” said the release of the four men should not be mistaken for a resolution of the wider concerns over the detention of its members. The group said its legal team had identified 83 people allegedly transferred from military custody at Wawa Barracks in Kainji, Niger State, to correctional facilities in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja. It claimed that its lawyers had communicated the names of legal representatives for the detainees to the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation. IPOB further alleged that several other people remained in detention, with some reportedly serving life sentences over cases linked to alleged membership of the group. Describing the situation as an abuse of state power, IPOB argued that political association or alleged membership of the organisation should not constitute grounds for imprisonment without proof of specific criminal offences. The group also questioned the legal basis of its proscription, arguing that the process was conducted through a civil ex parte proceeding and lacked the statutory approval required from the President under Section 2(1)(c) of the Terrorism (Prevention) Act 2013. It maintained that the signature of a Chief of Staff could not substitute for presidential approval where such approval was expressly required by law. IPOB cited the judgment in MultiChoice Nigeria Ltd v. FCCPC, involving Justice James Omotosho, to argue that statutory requirements should be applied consistently, irrespective of the parties involved. The group also referred to what it described as a subsisting inter partes ruling that IPOB was not an unlawful society, insisting that the government and prosecuting authorities should address the legal implications of the ruling. It disclosed that an appeal concerning the organisation’s status and the legality of its proscription was pending before the Supreme Court. IPOB argued that no individual should be sentenced to life imprisonment solely on the basis of alleged membership of the organisation, insisting that prosecutors must establish specific offences against each defendant. It maintained that the signature of a Chief of Staff could not substitute for presidential approval where such approval was expressly required by law. IPOB cited the judgment in MultiChoice Nigeria Ltd v. FCCPC, involving Justice James Omotosho, to argue that statutory requirements should be applied consistently, irrespective of the parties involved. The group also referred to what it described as a subsisting inter partes ruling that IPOB was not an unlawful society, insisting that the government and prosecuting authorities should address the legal implications of the ruling. It disclosed that an appeal concerning the organisation’s status and the legality of its proscription was pending before the Supreme Court. The group called on the Federal Government to account for the 83 people it said had been identified in correctional facilities in Keffi, Suleja and Kuje, as well as other people allegedly being held in connection with the Biafran agitation. It also urged the United Nations, the United States Government and the European Union to intervene over what it described as violations of the rights of detained Biafrans. “The release of the four is not the end of the matter. It is an indictment of the system that kept them imprisoned for four years,” the statement said. IPOB demanded the release of all people it considers unlawfully detained and an end to what it described as the criminalisation of its membership. item.title: Hardship: Northerners turn to cargo trucks for cheaper journeys despite risks
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-Aziz Usman, Damaturu POTISKUM — Despite Dangote’s ban on unauthorised passengers, Northerners still board its trucks to escape rising transport fares. In July 2026, Dangote Industries Limited offered N500,000 for credible information on illegal haulage, including unauthorised passenger transport, but travellers in Potiskum say rising fares leave them with few affordable options. Baba Iyatu, a middle-aged woman, was perched atop a Dangote compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered truck, among dozens of other passengers preparing to leave Potiskum, Yobe State. Her destination was Niger State, where her daughter had just given birth. For her, the journey was about family. But with the cost of conventional transport increasingly difficult to afford, reaching her daughter meant accepting the uncertainties of travelling on a truck designed to carry goods, not passengers. Baba Iyatu and the others knew the company prohibited unauthorised passengers on its trucks. Yet they argued that those enforcing the restrictions did not understand their economic circumstances. To them, the arrangement offered cheaper travel while giving drivers and their assistants opportunities to earn extra money. Their predicament captures a troubling reality in Nigeria: when the price of moving from one place to another becomes prohibitive, some people are willing to sacrifice comfort and safety to reach their destinations. The difference in cost is stark. Lagos fare A transport union worker known as agbero (name withheld), was interviewed at the ‘Tashan Na Tsira’ Motor Park in Potiskum, and he told the Arewa Voice correspondent that a bus journey from Potiskum to Lagos, which previously cost about N15,000, now costs approximately N35,000. By comparison, passengers can negotiate rides on heavy-duty trucks for between N5,000 and N10,000, depending on the driver’s mood. The difference can amount to as much as N30,000 on a single journey. For people already struggling with the cost of food, accommodation and other necessities, that saving can determine whether a journey is possible at all. Fuel prices have compounded the problem. In September 2026, petrol prices reached around N1,400 per litre in parts of Nigeria and N1,500 in some northern locations, while diesel exceeded N2,000 per litre, according to Reuters. Rising fuel costs add to the expenses facing transport operators, who must also contend with maintenance, spare parts and other running costs. But the passengers negotiating rides at Potiskum’s ‘Baban Tasha Park’ are not all travelling for the same reasons. Their stories reveal how the informal use of cargo trucks intersects with family obligations, unemployment and commercial activity. ‘I’ll think about job when I ge to Lagos’ Among those preparing to travel to Lagos was Adamu Hamisu, 24, who had secured a place on a privately owned truck transporting beans to the commercial city. It was his first trip to Lagos. He had arranged to stay with a friend but had no definite business plan. Asked what business he intended to start, Adamu said he would think about it once he arrived. For the young man, reaching Lagos came before deciding what to do there. He was travelling in search of greener pastures, hoping that being in the city would bring opportunities he could not readily access at home. His journey illustrates the uncertainty facing young people who leave their communities to seek work or start businesses without substantial resources. Spending less on transportation could leave them with more money for food, accommodation and the first steps towards earning a living. Hassan Idris, 34, was travelling for a different reason. The livestock trader was taking 14 rams to Lagos to sell. He had arranged with the truck driver to collect a few more animals in Azare, Bauchi State. Having traded livestock for five years, he already had accommodation arrangements in Lagos and middlemen who bought his animals for resale. Unlike Adamu, who was heading towards an uncertain future, Hassan was moving within an established commercial network connecting livestock traders in northern Nigeria with buyers in southern markets. Their journeys demonstrate how the use of cargo trucks extends beyond people simply trying to save money. The vehicles also form part of the wider movement of goods, traders and economic activity between communities. For the drivers and their assistants, however, the economics of the practice are different. Iliya, a truck driver’s assistant, explained that truck owners receive payment for delivering goods, while drivers and their assistants are settled for food and ‘calculated fuel expenses’. The assistants help deliver the cargo but do not necessarily receive the main payment for the job. Carrying passengers therefore offers another possible source of income. Sama’ila Ado, a truck driver who drove into ‘Tashan Yawale’, explained that drivers and their assistants also make money from selling used engine oil. According to him, the additional earnings form part of the informal arrangements through which they try to meet their daily needs while transporting goods over long distances. These accounts expose the competing pressures surrounding the practice. The truck owner has a commercial delivery to complete; the driver and assistant must manage the journey’s expenses; and passengers are looking for a cheaper way to travel. An arrangement that benefits one party financially, however, does not automatically make it safe or permissible. The dangers begin with the conditions in which passengers travel. Those riding in open truck compartments or perched atop cargo have little protection from rain, dust and harsh weather. They also face the risks associated with sudden braking, vehicle instability and road accidents. For Baba Iyatu, the journey was a means of reaching her daughter and newborn grandchild. But the emotional importance of that visit could not remove the physical risks of travelling in a vehicle designed to carry goods rather than people. Drivers also contend with difficulties that can make long-distance haulage more expensive and unpredictable. Sama’ila described bad roads, rain and encounters with people who block roads and demand money from drivers. Such accounts point to additional pressures on transport operators, although the locations and circumstances of the reported incidents require further verification. Poor road conditions can delay deliveries, increase vehicle maintenance costs and leave drivers exposed to breakdowns far from assistance. For operators already managing fuel and food expenses, delays and unexpected payments can further complicate the economics of a journey. Dangote’s rule on truck Dangote’s restrictions add another dimension to the problem. In July 2026, Dangote Industries Limited (DIL) announced a whistleblowing initiative offering N500,000 for credible information leading to action against the unauthorised use of its branded trucks, including the transportation of unauthorised goods and passengers. The company said the initiative was intended to protect its logistics operations and ensure that its trucks carried only approved cargo. The company also said law enforcement agencies, including the police, had been authorised to arrest drivers found using its trucks for unauthorised commercial haulage. The presence of passengers on the Dangote-branded truck observed in Potiskum therefore raises questions about how the restrictions are enforced and why some travellers continue to accept the risks. The observation establishes that passengers were aboard the truck; it does not, by itself, establish the identity of the truck’s operator or whether the company was aware of that particular journey. For passengers, the immediate concern is the price of reaching their destinations. For the company, unauthorised use of its vehicles raises questions of compliance, operational control and liability.
