item.title: High Court Ruling: AA candidate warns against weakening opposition
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The presidential candidate of the Action Alliance (AA), Faduri Oluwadare Joseph, has warned that increasing judicial involvement in political party disputes could undermine democratic participation and weaken opposition politics ahead of the 2027 general elections. Joseph, popularly known as Fadojoe, expressed concern over the implications of the Federal High Court judgment concerning the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the presidential nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. In a statement issued under his Operation Rescue Nigeria 2027 platform, the AA candidate said the judgment had raised questions about the independence of the judiciary, the future of political competition and the state of Nigeria’s democracy. He said his intervention was not motivated by membership of the ADC but by the need to protect democratic participation and the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. According to him, an injustice against democratic participation in one political party could eventually affect other parties and candidates. “Today, it is Atiku Abubakar and the ADC. Tomorrow, it could be Peter Obi, myself, or any other opposition candidate,” he said. Joseph maintained that although political parties and candidates must operate within the law, the judiciary should ensure that its decisions did not undermine the fundamental principles of democratic participation. He expressed concern over what he described as a growing trend of political parties spending more time in courtrooms defending their leadership structures and electoral rights than presenting their programmes to Nigerians. The AA candidate also questioned the increasing influence of internal party disputes, prolonged litigation and conflicting judicial interpretations on the electoral process. He argued that courtrooms should not become substitutes for ballot boxes, insisting that the judiciary must protect justice and public confidence in the democratic process. Joseph further raised concerns about the state of opposition politics under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, citing persistent leadership disputes, factional disagreements and legal battles involving opposition parties. He noted that the ADC had accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to weaken the opposition through legal processes, but stressed that such allegations required independent examination. The presidential candidate urged Tinubu and the APC to recognise the importance of a strong opposition in sustaining democratic governance. He recalled Tinubu’s involvement in the pro-democracy struggle against military rule, particularly the activities of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), arguing that democratic freedoms should be protected regardless of political affiliation. item.title: 2027: Peter Obi is a trader, he hasn’t offered any alternative — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has described the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, as a trader who has failed to present an alternative to President Bola Tinubu’s policies ahead of the 2027 general election. Oshiomhole made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, arguing that Obi’s approach to governance was driven by short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. The former Edo State governor said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest the presidency but maintained that Tinubu deserved another term after overcoming the initial challenges of his administration. According to Oshiomhole, Nigerians should allow the President to continue rather than “recruit a new apprentice”. He also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The senator framed the 2027 election as a choice between Tinubu’s economic policies and those of Atiku, whom he accused of presiding over a system of multiple exchange rates that favoured people based on their connections. Oshiomhole defended the Tinubu administration’s workers’ welfare policies, citing the approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance as evidence that the President cared about ordinary Nigerians. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress on October 27. The agreement also provides for outstanding peculiar allowances to be paid in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. The post 2027: Peter Obi is a trader, he hasn’t offered any alternative — Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Key takeaways from 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit
item.description: By Emeka Anaeto, Business Editor The 32nd edition of Nigerian Economic Summit held last week in Abuja has produced one of the most critical insights and engagements across stakeholders in Nigeria’s economy spanning across public and private sector. It also delivered some thought provoking contents on what is wrong with economic development in the country across policy strategies and execution imperatives. With significant dose of international personalities with experiences across the world, the discussions were frank and unpatronising of any vested interest. Themed, ‘‘Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity’’, the cardinal objectives were anchored on the three-and-half years of President Bola Tinubu’s massive economic reform which has already become controversial ahead of the next general elections in the country. The gathering of distinguished global leaders, senior government officials across the Federal and State levels, private sector executives, economists, and development partners were set to build consensus on practical pathways for accelerating inclusive and sustainable growth. The NES#32 actually provided platform for translating reform momentum into tangible outcomes that could expand productive employment, raise productivity and ensure shared prosperity. Furthermore, the Summit dissected Nigeria’s development priorities across five critical sub-themes, including: Work Nigeria, which entails building a job-rich and strengthening labour absorption; Produce Nigeria, which entails driving productivity, industrialization, and value creation; Invest Nigeria, which entails delivering investment, shared prosperity, welfare, and social protection; Scale Nigeria , which entails expanding growth across states, sectors, and communities; and Secure Nigeria which entails restoring safety, stability, and confidence for economic activities. The key takeaways from the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit show the outcome reinforced one overriding national imperative: ‘Nigeria must move decisively from macroeconomic stabilisation and policy reform to measurable economic prosperity, productive employment and improved living standards for its citizens’. The discussions acknowledged progress towards macroeconomic stability while emphasising that growth must translate into improved household incomes, greater business competitiveness, food security, stronger institutions and broader economic opportunities. item.content:encoded: By Emeka Anaeto, Business Editor The 32nd edition of Nigerian Economic Summit held last week in Abuja has produced one of the most critical insights and engagements across stakeholders in Nigeria’s economy spanning across public and private sector. It also delivered some thought provoking contents on what is wrong with economic development in the country across policy strategies and execution imperatives. With significant dose of international personalities with experiences across the world, the discussions were frank and unpatronising of any vested interest. Themed, ‘‘Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity’’, the cardinal objectives were anchored on the three-and-half years of President Bola Tinubu’s massive economic reform which has already become controversial ahead of the next general elections in the country. The gathering of distinguished global leaders, senior government officials across the Federal and State levels, private sector executives, economists, and development partners were set to build consensus on practical pathways for accelerating inclusive and sustainable growth. The NES#32 actually provided platform for translating reform momentum into tangible outcomes that could expand productive employment, raise productivity and ensure shared prosperity. Furthermore, the Summit dissected Nigeria’s development priorities across five critical sub-themes, including: Work Nigeria, which entails building a job-rich and strengthening labour absorption; Produce Nigeria, which entails driving productivity, industrialization, and value creation; Invest Nigeria, which entails delivering investment, shared prosperity, welfare, and social protection; Scale Nigeria , which entails expanding growth across states, sectors, and communities; and Secure Nigeria which entails restoring safety, stability, and confidence for economic activities. The key takeaways from the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit show the outcome reinforced one overriding national imperative: ‘Nigeria must move decisively from macroeconomic stabilisation and policy reform to measurable economic prosperity, productive employment and improved living standards for its citizens’. The discussions acknowledged progress towards macroeconomic stability while emphasising that growth must translate into improved household incomes, greater business competitiveness, food security, stronger institutions and broader economic opportunities. Reforms performance presents a mixed picture – NESG Chairman Welcoming the array of Nigerian business elites at the thirty-second edition of the Nigeria Economic Summit in Abuja yesterday, the Chairman of NESG, Mr Niyi Yusuf, said though the reforms have presented a form of stability but he declared that stabilization may create conditions for economic progress but doesn’t deliver it. Dissecting the major outcomes from the reforms so far, Yusuf stated: “Nigeria’s economic performance presents a mixed picture. Key macro indicators are improving, but significant constraints limit the transmission of these gains to businesses and households. He further noted, “Nigeria attracted approximately US$23.2 billion in foreign capital inflows so far in 2026, but portfolio investment dominated, with foreign direct investment only a small proportion. Giving NESG’s overall position on the performance of the reforms so far, Yusuf stated: “These reforms have imposed considerable pressures on households and businesses, but they have also created an opportunity to reconsider the foundations of our socio-economic development. “Our responsibility now is to ensure that reform translates into stronger enterprises, better jobs, more productive workers, rising incomes, improved living standards and shared prosperity. This is the central purpose of NES #32. No other way than reforms – Tinubu Speaking to the global audience about the reforms’ imperatives and deliveries, President Bola Tinubu, through his deputy, Vice President Kashim Shettima, said the administration is currently undertaking what it came into office to achieve: rewriting the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long. ‎He noted that his administration began on a difficult note because there is no shortcut to economic growth. These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth,” he added, noting that the administration is encouraged by what it has accomplished so far. ‎”We must judge industrial policy by the competitiveness of our firms and investment incentives by the capital, technology, exports and jobs they attract.” ‎On economic diversification, he stated that “non-oil activities accounted for 96.08% of GDP, while manufacturing grew by 3.29% and the oil sector by 2.57%,” emphasising that the gains have reinforced his administration’s confidence in the path of recovery and diversification. ‎Giving more performance highlights of the administration the President stated: “In the first quarter of 2026, our capital importation reached $10.37 billion, an increase of 83.83% over the corresponding period in 2025. This comprised both portfolio and foreign direct investment. We will, therefore, continue to ease regulatory burdens, strengthen transparency and policy predictability, and expand access to finance. Conditions for Nigeria to achieve sustainable economic growth – Prof Dercon Speaking on how Nigeria could move from economic stabilisation to sustained growth, Professor Stefan Dercon of the University of Oxford, United Kingdom, who delivered the keynote speech, stated: ‘‘For Nigeria to achieve sustainable economic growth, its political, business, military and civil service elite must forge a common front, abandon the status quo and commit to a development agenda’. that serves the broader national interest. Dercon warned that the process would not be easy because those benefiting from the existing system were likely to resist changes that threatened their interests. He said Nigeria needed a coalition of influential groups committed to economic expansion, peace and stability, rather than a system that primarily protected the interests of a privileged few. 10 strategic outcomes From the deliberations documented, ten strategic outcomes and priorities emerge: 1. A New Economic Accord for Inclusive and Sustainable Growth: The Summit underscored the need for a durable economic accord that institutionalises reforms beyond political and electoral cycles. Discussions called for stronger policy consistency, improved federal–state coordination, export-led growth and increased productive investment. The objective is to move beyond economic growth of approximately 4% towards the 7–9% growth considered necessary to accelerate poverty reduction, while raising investment from approximately 17–20% towards 30–40% of national output. 2. Accelerating Trade Competitiveness and Regional Integration: The Summit identified trade facilitation as essential to unlocking the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Priorities include modernising ports, reducing border delays, introducing one-stop border posts, improving multimodal logistics and removing non-tariff barriers. Particular emphasis was placed on developing competitive regional value chains in agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, building materials and light manufacturing, alongside stronger market access for MSMEs and women traders. 3. Unlocking MSMEs and the Informal Economy: A central message was that Nigeria’s informal economy should be treated as a productive national asset rather than merely a regulatory challenge. The discussions advocated incentive based formalisation, affordable and appropriately structured financing, stronger industrial supply-chain linkages, improved market access and sustained business-development support. MSME interventions should be data-driven, responsive to different business growth

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 6 – A Farewell to Swift
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 6 – A… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Farewell to Swift Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA ‘s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory . After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia . The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite’s Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope . Swift had a combination of instruments, including an X-ray telescope and a gamma-ray telescope , that worked together to enable humanity to study, in unprecedented detail, the fastest and most energetic explosions in the universe. The most recent solar maximum accelerated the decay of the satellite’s orbit. An innovative mission to rescue Swift by boosting its orbit was not successful . Swift burned on reentry like a shooting star, but the impressive data acquired by the telescope over its mission will continue to bring light to the mysteries of the cosmos for years to come. May it keep inspiring new missions to boldly go into space, explore new data and seek out new science. Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? Date November 6, 2026 Credit NASA / Swift and AndreaMosaic Authors & editors: Cecilia Chirenti, Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC , NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. May it keep inspiring new missions to boldly go into space, explore new data and seek out new science. Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? item.title: Taking a Gander at Utah’s Goosenecks
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Taking a Gander at Utah’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 6, 2026 Tens of millions of years ago, the San Juan River in what is now southern Utah shared some characteristics with today’s Mississippi River. In a bygone geologic era, the San Juan flowed across a relatively flat plain that formed in an ancient marine environment. Unencumbered by rugged terrain, the river was free to take a long, meandering path on its gradual journey downslope. But this part of the San Juan changed when geologic forces pushed the Colorado Plateau upward. Some experts think that within the later stages of this “ still-enigmatic ” history, starting around 20 million years ago, the plateau’s rise elevated the San Juan’s headwaters , which increased the river’s gradient and sped its flow. With that, the water’s erosive power intensified, and the river started carving its winding path deeper and deeper through 300-million-year-old rock. Today, on its westward path to Lake Powell, the San Juan River flows through an impressive series of entrenched meanders, also known as “goosenecks.” An astronaut aboard the International Space Station photographed the stark desert topography on October 6, 2026. In Utah’s Goosenecks State Park , the river runs through a canyon 1,000 feet (300 meters) deep. In places, it nearly loops back on itself, making horseshoe-shaped bends. One section is so curvy that the river travels 5.5 miles (8.9 kilometers) between two points that are only 1.3 miles (2.1 kilometers) apart as the crow—nay, goose—flies. Entrenched meanders in Utah’s Goosenecks State Park are bathed in golden light on August 8, 2016. Photo by Bob Wick (BLM) While the goosenecks are an unusual geologic wonder to behold by day, the area’s dark skies are a spectacle by night. Goosenecks State Park’s remote, high-desert location and 360-degree views of the sky helped earn it an International Dark Sky Park designation in 2021. According to DarkSky International, features such as the Double Cluster in Perseus and the Messier 24 star cloud in the Sagittarius spiral arm of the Milky Way are visible to the unaided eye from the park. In November 2026 , dark skies offer the chance to view several meteor showers, with the Northern Taurids, Southern Taurids, and Leonids reaching their peaks throughout the month. Astronaut photograph ISS075-E-188830 was acquired on October 6, 2026, with a Nikon Z9 digital camera using a focal length of 400 millimeters. It is provided by the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility and the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit at NASA Johnson Space Center. The image was

item.title: AI agents are a ‘bane’ for some website operators, says Cloudflare
item.description: Nation-state actors and criminals likely exploited the PHP2SHELL vulnerability before its disclosure, according to Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince. “These vulnerabilities, like the PHP vulnerabilities that were disclosed the other day, had been in the wild for years,” Prince said on the company’s third quarter earnings call. “We're going back through our logs looking for any evidence that hackers or nation-state actors or others had been using them in the past. I know that we're going to find examples of that.” That was just one of the warnings he offered on the call, among them that some of Cloudflare’s customers believe AI agents are “a bane to their business and want to keep them away.” To explain why, Prince hypothesized that he could use an agent to find him a restaurant to eat at after he finishes his day of investor relations duties. “It might go and scour the internet and look at 1,000 different restaurants' websites, pull down 1,000 different menus, and then I might choose to only go to one of those,” he said. “The problem is that 999 of those restaurants have now had a cost that is just been applied to them, but they are not getting any benefit.” The CEO admitted that web searches have always driven some low-value traffic but feels the volume of agentic activity – which Cloudflare has previously predicted will be one thousand times greater than clicks from humans – means the problem is now at a different scale. Prince also had bad news for Kubernetes aficionados, because he thinks containers might become another casualty of the agentic age. The CEO allowed that containers are “a significant improvement over bare metal or even virtual machines,” and said they fueled the growth of hyperscale clouds and mobile applications. But he thinks containers are already cooked. “The container-based architecture of the hyperscalers and neoclouds just can't keep up in a cost-effective way with the new agentic paradigms of today,” he argued, again citing the 1000:1 ratio of bot:human traffic Cloudflare expects to see online any year now. That’s a Cloudflare-centric view, because Prince pitched the company’s serverless “Workers” service as an alternative to containers. The company also offers products that can either block agents, ameliorate the cost and traffic impacts of agentic activity, or allow organizations to monetize traffic generated by AI. Prince said demand for those products is growing fast, claiming that since July 1 st , “approximately five percent” of the web opted in to Cloudflare’s content protection products. The CEO said Meta is already a customer, and said Zuck’s new “Muse” agents will benefit Cloudflare by creating more agentic traffic that third parties want to tame. He also pointed to year-on-year revenue growth of 39 percent, which saw quarterly revenue reach a record $782.5 million. item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: Nation-state actors and criminals likely exploited the PHP2SHELL vulnerability before its disclosure, according to Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince. “These vulnerabilities, like the PHP vulnerabilities that were disclosed the other day, had been in the wild for years,” Prince said on the company’s third quarter earnings call. “We're going back through our logs looking for any evidence that hackers or nation-state actors or others had been using them in the past. I know that we're going to find examples of that.” That was just one of the warnings he offered on the call, among them that some of Cloudflare’s customers believe AI agents are “a bane to their business and want to keep them away.” To explain why, Prince hypothesized that he could use an agent to find him a restaurant to eat at after he finishes his day of investor relations duties. “It might go and scour the internet and look at 1,000 different restaurants' websites, pull down 1,000 different menus, and then I might choose to only go to one of those,” he said. “The problem is that 999 of those restaurants have now had a cost that is just been applied to them, but they are not getting any benefit.” The CEO admitted that web searches have always driven some low-value traffic but feels the volume of agentic activity – which Cloudflare has previously predicted will be one thousand times greater than clicks from humans – means the problem is now at a different scale. Prince also had bad news for Kubernetes aficionados, because he thinks containers might become another casualty of the agentic age. The CEO allowed that containers are “a significant improvement over bare metal or even virtual machines,” and said they fueled the growth of hyperscale clouds and mobile applications. But he thinks containers are already cooked. “The container-based architecture of the hyperscalers and neoclouds just can't keep up in a cost-effective way with the new agentic paradigms of today,” he argued, again citing the 1000:1 ratio of bot:human traffic Cloudflare expects to see online any year now. That’s a Cloudflare-centric view, because Prince pitched the company’s serverless “Workers” service as an alternative to containers. The company also offers products that can either block agents, ameliorate the cost and traffic impacts of agentic activity, or allow organizations to monetize traffic generated by AI. Prince said demand for those products is growing fast, claiming that since July 1 st , “approximately five percent” of the web opted in to Cloudflare’s content protection products. The CEO said Meta is already a customer, and said Zuck’s new “Muse” agents will benefit Cloudflare by creating more agentic traffic that third parties want to tame. He also pointed to year-on-year revenue growth of 39 percent, which saw quarterly revenue reach a record $782.5 million. And he thinks there are better days ahead, due to the terrible state of security. “It may seem like the sky is falling with the number of new security vulnerabilities that have been reported over the last few weeks,” Prince said. “I wish I could tell you we were through the worst, but we're not.” He thinks Cloudflare can profit from security misery because the extent of its activities and client base mean it is “among the first to receive quiet disclosure of new vulnerabilities” and remediates them before disclosure. Investors thought this all made sense, and in after-hours trading sent Cloudflare shares up by around 15 percent, meaning it recovered and then improved on losses that it incurred earlier after major US indices dropped around four percent as investors who worry tech stocks are overvalued. ®

item.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
item.description: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. Vendors of observability tools will be warming up their Indian sales teams today, because CERT-IN’s advice to Indian businesses includes improving their ability to log events, monitor for anomalies in real time, and send alerts. It also urged keeping test environments off the internet, and restricting access to cloud resources because CRAFTY FALCON is fond of using them to run its attacks. CERT-IN also warns that the attacks are “active and escalating” and therefore worthy of 24x7 monitoring. Interestingly, the CERT’s advisory mentions attacks on “entities” across banking, financial services, and insurance, but only names the kind of businesses mentioned above as having reported attacks. The Register points this out because India is home to literally thousands of banks, many of them small operations that sometimes lack basic infosec protections . CRAFTY FALCON therefore has a target-rich environment in India should it choose to expand its activities. ®

item.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
item.description: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations. One connection, works every time, needs no retries There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
item.description: NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years. The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” Isaacman said. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Feds warn grocers: Don't chill on cyber defenses as freezer hacking spree heats up
item.description: If you have any industrial smart freezers, look out. The US federal government is urging owners and operators to disconnect them from the internet, apply patches, change default passwords, and take other security measures to prevent the kind of attacks that have become prevalent in Europe. “We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. Since mid-October, unknown miscreants have hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores in France, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden. The attacks increase the temperature inside fridges to highs of 50ºC (122°F), spoiling food, and sparking fires. The Register asked the FBI if it has documented any successful or attempted attacks against refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems in America. We had not received a response to our questions at the time of publication, nor are we aware of any documented digital attacks against these systems in American supermarkets. But there are signs that stateside operators are aware of the issue. Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, last month said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack that affected most of its US and European brands. Delhaize supermarkets in Europe are among those hit by the destructive freezer attacks. The Pentagon is also reportedly treating a series of freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the US in August as a suspected cyberattack, according to Reuters, which cited four officials familiar with the matter. In a Thursday advisory, the US FBI, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Health and Human Services, and departments of Agriculture and Transportation warned organizations about the ongoing cyber threats facing operators of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies said . Attackers exploit these flaws by bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and abusing weak configurations, according to the feds. Once criminals gain access to the systems, they can change the temperature to spoil food or temperature-controlled medications, start fires, and ultimately harm people who consume products that haven’t been stored at proper temperatures. How to stay frosty To prevent these scenarios, the government organizations urge owners and operators to “immediately” implement best practices and security protections. First and foremost on the list: do not expose industrial control systems and devices to the public internet. Ira
item.dc:creator: Jessica Lyons
item.content:encoded: If you have any industrial smart freezers, look out. The US federal government is urging owners and operators to disconnect them from the internet, apply patches, change default passwords, and take other security measures to prevent the kind of attacks that have become prevalent in Europe. “We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. Since mid-October, unknown miscreants have hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores in France, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden. The attacks increase the temperature inside fridges to highs of 50ºC (122°F), spoiling food, and sparking fires. The Register asked the FBI if it has documented any successful or attempted attacks against refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems in America. We had not received a response to our questions at the time of publication, nor are we aware of any documented digital attacks against these systems in American supermarkets. But there are signs that stateside operators are aware of the issue. Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, last month said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack that affected most of its US and European brands. Delhaize supermarkets in Europe are among those hit by the destructive freezer attacks. The Pentagon is also reportedly treating a series of freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the US in August as a suspected cyberattack, according to Reuters, which cited four officials familiar with the matter. In a Thursday advisory, the US FBI, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Health and Human Services, and departments of Agriculture and Transportation warned organizations about the ongoing cyber threats facing operators of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies said . Attackers exploit these flaws by bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and abusing weak configurations, according to the feds. Once criminals gain access to the systems, they can change the temperature to spoil food or temperature-controlled medications, start fires, and ultimately harm people who consume products that haven’t been stored at proper temperatures. How to stay frosty To prevent these scenarios, the government organizations urge owners and operators to “immediately” implement best practices and security protections. First and foremost on the list: do not expose industrial control systems and devices to the public internet. Iranian hackers used internet-accessible programmable logic controllers (PLCs) to break into more than 100 US water systems in July. This sort of exposed device, which often lacks password protection, is a boon to miscreants looking for an easy button to gain access to critical facilities . “Should remote access be necessary, protect it by using a firewall or edge device and updating it to the latest version to reduce security vulnerabilities,” the feds advise. Other recommended tactics include: Create a dedicated VLAN for operational technology (OT) devices, to isolate industrial devices from business networks. Replace default passwords with strong passwords and policies, turning on phishing-resistant multifactor authentication (MFA) whenever possible. Apply patches in a timely manner, and retire and replace legacy devices that no longer receive security updates from the manufacturer. Define and maintain a device and IP allow-list, and limit access to OT devices to only those on the list. Maintain and test backups. These should be kept offsite and offline. And finally: enable logging and regularly review logs for any unusual activity.®

item.title: Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words
item.description: The former midfielder with impressive managerial promotion record began with a thrilling comeback in draw at Cardiff Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon. “It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.” Continue reading...

item.title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
item.description: Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use. Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer , an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates "build on top" of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete "ongoing, large-scale work." You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously - much like OpenAI's Dots and Claude Duet . Perple … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: AWS Kiro aims to solve identity crisis by adding another identity: bot orchestrator
item.description: AWS Kiro, the cloud giant's AI-oriented integrated development environment, isn't the most popular code editor. That honor goes to Microsoft's Visual Studio Code, at least as measured by Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey . Kiro might rank 27th among the listed IDEs, but then it's not really an IDE anymore. Having shrugged off reports that it played a role in outages last year, Kiro now styles itself "an agentic development environment" after a brief stint as " an agentic IDE ." It's also the inheritor of Amazon Q Developer coding assistant users, who have been directed to migrate to Kiro . It's also " an AI-powered development environment that helps you build software from prototype to production." It's "available as a desktop IDE, a command-line interface, a web app, a mobile app, and a personal AI agent (Crew)." Except that Kiro Crew is also "the persistent, open source development workspace." It's more agent infrastructure – an environment – that supports Kiro Web , IDE , and CLI . To help get Kiro through its identity crisis and perhaps make it more beloved, AWS is expanding Kiro's remit still further. The cloud giant is launching Kiro Crew bots, recalling similar efforts like OpenAI dots and Grok Bot , as well as Claude Duet and Meta Muse. Bots in Kiro Crew are software agents that attempt to carry out long-running tasks. "A bot is a new way to structure and drive agentic work," a Kiro blog post explains. "Instead of working in isolated sessions, each bot is a named, long-running agent that you define and customize for a specific part of your work. It has its own memory and runs its own sessions so you stop tracking them one by one. Kiro Crew already learns from how you work. Bots change where that learning lives." There's some appealing anthropomorphism to giving each agent a name and its own tools, permissions, and memories. You're suddenly surrounded by friends. The possible downside is how that gets billed – there's potential for a lot of duplicated context if your many agents process overlapping data without some form of shared cache. Given Amazon's concerns about internal token usage and developer complaints about runaway costs in Kiro, it seems other organizations might be curious about the potential expense of keeping bot memory isolated. In response to our inquiry about the cost of keeping memory separate, an AWS spokesperson said, “All of the Kiro bots bill together through a developer’s existing Kiro plan. Each bot in Kiro Crew has its own memory and sessions, and their learned context is intentionally kept separate so that what one bot learns doesn’t bleed into another’s work. However, all bots operate within the same Kiro Crew workspace, use the same harness, and have access to the same codebase, project files, MCP, skills, and tools—so they don’t need to independently rediscover your project structure.” In any event, figuring out how Kiro Crew agents are spending tokens looks likely to require analytics of some sort, becau
item.dc:creator: Thomas Claburn
item.content:encoded: AWS Kiro, the cloud giant's AI-oriented integrated development environment, isn't the most popular code editor. That honor goes to Microsoft's Visual Studio Code, at least as measured by Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey . Kiro might rank 27th among the listed IDEs, but then it's not really an IDE anymore. Having shrugged off reports that it played a role in outages last year, Kiro now styles itself "an agentic development environment" after a brief stint as " an agentic IDE ." It's also the inheritor of Amazon Q Developer coding assistant users, who have been directed to migrate to Kiro . It's also " an AI-powered development environment that helps you build software from prototype to production." It's "available as a desktop IDE, a command-line interface, a web app, a mobile app, and a personal AI agent (Crew)." Except that Kiro Crew is also "the persistent, open source development workspace." It's more agent infrastructure – an environment – that supports Kiro Web , IDE , and CLI . To help get Kiro through its identity crisis and perhaps make it more beloved, AWS is expanding Kiro's remit still further. The cloud giant is launching Kiro Crew bots, recalling similar efforts like OpenAI dots and Grok Bot , as well as Claude Duet and Meta Muse. Bots in Kiro Crew are software agents that attempt to carry out long-running tasks. "A bot is a new way to structure and drive agentic work," a Kiro blog post explains. "Instead of working in isolated sessions, each bot is a named, long-running agent that you define and customize for a specific part of your work. It has its own memory and runs its own sessions so you stop tracking them one by one. Kiro Crew already learns from how you work. Bots change where that learning lives." There's some appealing anthropomorphism to giving each agent a name and its own tools, permissions, and memories. You're suddenly surrounded by friends. The possible downside is how that gets billed – there's potential for a lot of duplicated context if your many agents process overlapping data without some form of shared cache. Given Amazon's concerns about internal token usage and developer complaints about runaway costs in Kiro, it seems other organizations might be curious about the potential expense of keeping bot memory isolated. In response to our inquiry about the cost of keeping memory separate, an AWS spokesperson said, “All of the Kiro bots bill together through a developer’s existing Kiro plan. Each bot in Kiro Crew has its own memory and sessions, and their learned context is intentionally kept separate so that what one bot learns doesn’t bleed into another’s work. However, all bots operate within the same Kiro Crew workspace, use the same harness, and have access to the same codebase, project files, MCP, skills, and tools—so they don’t need to independently rediscover your project structure.” In any event, figuring out how Kiro Crew agents are spending tokens looks likely to require analytics of some sort, because AWS Kiro subscriptions are sold as " credits " that get converted to tokens at different rates, depending on the underlying model. As a thought experiment, AWS suggests a developer might deploy an intake bot for reading trouble or job tickets, labeling them, flagging duplicates, and drafting reproduction steps for bugs. Then there might be the build-health bot for checking the CI pipeline periodically and surfacing test failures that require the attention made scarce by having to deal with a bunch of AI agents. A code review bot might also be warranted for reviewing pull requests and other delegated responsibilities. And top that off with a release-readiness bot, for confirming that merged changes have tests and for seeking release sign-off. For those smitten by the idea of a single surface through which multiple agents can be configured, routed, and governed, Kiro Crew has your backend. ®

item.title: Salon is shutting down after 31 years
item.description: Salon launched 31 years ago as one of the first online-only news magazine outlets, and it announced today in an unsigned post that it's ceasing publication. The company said that the "business realities of independent digital journalism have changed profoundly over the years," and it decided that its publishing model is "no longer sustainable." It didn't go into detail about why, but many websites are grappling with "Google Zero" and the impact of AI tools . When reached for comment, Salon general manager Amanda Wolfe pointed The Verge to today's announcement post. item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. Continue reading...

item.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
item.description: null Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon (at far right) is seen at the base of the newly-deployed eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit. Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem. "We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy." To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment. Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue. "We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk (at center) works on mounting the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes. "Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. Half the size of the old ones and bringing 40% more power." NASA graphic showing the location and power channel
item.dc:creator: Robert Z. Pearlman
item.content:encoded: null Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon (at far right) is seen at the base of the newly-deployed eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit. Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem. "We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy." To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment. Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue. "We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk (at center) works on mounting the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes. "Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. Half the size of the old ones and bringing 40% more power." NASA graphic showing the location and power channel for all eight now-deployed International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays (iROSAs). (Image credit: NASA) Each of the eight iROSAs and their mounting assemblies were delivered to the space station by SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft. Beginning in June 2021, four teams of two astronauts did as was done on Thursday to deploy each array. In addition to Kutryk and Menon's work on the 2A and 3B power channels, the spacewalkers included Shane Kimbrough of NASA and Thomas Pesquet of the European Space Agency for the 2B and 4B channels; Josh Cassada and Frank Rubio, both with NASA, on 3A and 4A in December 2022; and NASA's Steve Bowen and Woody Hoburg on 1A and 1B in June 2023. The need for the iROSA augmentations was discovered by flight controllers when the space station's eight original arrays began to show degraded power output as they exceeded their 15-year design life. The iROSAs provide the additional electricity needed to support ISS operations through its retirement and controlled deorbit , which are currently scheduled to occur in late 2030. "Congratulations to you all on your stellar work to finish the last of the roll-out solar arrays and the upgrades to the ISS power system that will take it to the end of its journey," said Stilwell, addressing Menon and Kutryk. "It is fitting that we just surpassed 26 years of constant human presence on the International Space Station , and you all showed us what the best of humanity looks like executing one of the most difficult and dangerous [things] humans do and making it look easy. Congratulations!" Menon has now logged 33 hours and 30 minutes on four spacewalks, while Kutryk has tailed 14 hours and 10 minutes on two EVAs. Thursday's spacewalk was the 101st U.S. EVA at the International Space Station without a space shuttle being present and the 286th overall in support of ISS assembly, maintenance and upgrades. It was the ninth spacewalk of 2026 and the sixth conducted by the station's 75th resident crew.

item.title: 3 Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Movies You Can Stream For Free This Weekend (Novemeber 6 - 8)
item.description: Science Fiction as a genre is one that fans get to explore in many different ways. Whether it is a horror movie or a comedy, elements of science fiction can turn a story into something so memorable for fans. And sometimes, you just want to watch a movie that has something a little more to it for you to unpack. The problem is trying to figure out what the best science fiction movie is to watch and with a large library of the genre online, picking the best of the best isn't easy.

item.title: Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview)
item.description: null Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements. "One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone," states the official synopsis. "When a quantum anomaly tears apart the starship Wild Blue Yonder, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time." Ahead of the audio drama's launch, we sat down with Weir and Percy to find out more about this exciting science fiction adventure. Andy Weir has already been responsible for one sci-fi hit this year, as his novel "Project Hail Mary" received a stunning movie adaptation starring Ryan Gosling. (Image credit: Getty Images (Dimitrios Kambouris)) When Percy was first approached by Audible about this challenging endeavor, it was part of a bake-off situation where he was competing with several other writers, all jockeying for position. "I think the thing that set me apart is my understanding of how to channel legacy properties," Percy tells Space. "Having written for DC and for Marvel, I can take 'Star Wars' or 'Predator' or Wolverine or Batman and honor that legacy but also put my own unique spin on it. "When it came to the banner of 'Andy Weir Presents,' my job was to write my best version of an awesome Andy Weir story. So I thought about space disasters, big-hearted hopefulness, quippy humor, and a roller coaster plot, and then I nested into all of that a time-travel story." Writing an audio drama is unlike the comic work that Percy is known for, but as he explains, it's also quite different from working on conventional shows and movies too. "If you’re watching TV or film, you’re passive and letting it wash over you. You’re taking in the story as a passenger," notes Percy. "But when you're listening to audio, you're invited in with the dialogue, the narration, the sound cues. You’re invited to fill in the vacancies. As a result of that, you become like a co-author in the experience. I was super excited to jump into this project." "Exoplanet" lands on Nov. 5, 2026 exclusively on Audible (Image credit: Audible) The genesis of "Exoplanet" started with Audible approaching Weir with the basic idea, but what they didn't know was that he had already been thinking about resurrecting great radio

"When a quantum anomaly tears apart the starship Wild Blue Yonder, each surviving crew member crash-lands in a different era on the same deadly exoplanet—hunted, alone, and running out of time." Ahead of the audio drama's launch, we sat down with Weir and Percy to find out more about this exciting science fiction adventure. Andy Weir has already been responsible for one sci-fi hit this year, as his novel "Project Hail Mary" received a stunning movie adaptation starring Ryan Gosling. (Image credit: Getty Images (Dimitrios Kambouris)) When Percy was first approached by Audible about this challenging endeavor, it was part of a bake-off situation where he was competing with several other writers, all jockeying for position. "I think the thing that set me apart is my understanding of how to channel legacy properties," Percy tells Space. "Having written for DC and for Marvel, I can take 'Star Wars' or 'Predator' or Wolverine or Batman and honor that legacy but also put my own unique spin on it. "When it came to the banner of 'Andy Weir Presents,' my job was to write my best version of an awesome Andy Weir story. So I thought about space disasters, big-hearted hopefulness, quippy humor, and a roller coaster plot, and then I nested into all of that a time-travel story." Writing an audio drama is unlike the comic work that Percy is known for, but as he explains, it's also quite different from working on conventional shows and movies too. "If you’re watching TV or film, you’re passive and letting it wash over you. You’re taking in the story as a passenger," notes Percy. "But when you're listening to audio, you're invited in with the dialogue, the narration, the sound cues. You’re invited to fill in the vacancies. As a result of that, you become like a co-author in the experience. I was super excited to jump into this project." "Exoplanet" lands on Nov. 5, 2026 exclusively on Audible (Image credit: Audible) The genesis of "Exoplanet" started with Audible approaching Weir with the basic idea, but what they didn't know was that he had already been thinking about resurrecting great radio dramas of the past. "Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment with full-cast productions and sound effects," shares Weir. "I got into listening to things like 'The Lone Ranger' and 'The Shadow' and, of course, the Basil Rathbone Sherlock Holmes adaptations. Also, 'Zorro' was a radio show, and there were a lot of good westerns. "At the time, I wasn't yet famous or a writer, but I thought I could do this myself. I could write something, narrate it, throw in some sound effects, and put it up online," Weir recalls. "But then I didn't because I’m really lazy. Then many moons later, Audible comes up to me, and I have an opportunity to participate in that exact thing. I especially like the part where all the hard work is done by Ben. That’s my favorite part." Exoplanet's all-star cast features Ariana DeBose, Anthony Mackie, and John Leguizamo. (Image credit: Getty Images) As Weir points out, he's thankfully not the one wielding the pen this time around, but he did select Percy to be his champion. "We got a bunch of different story concepts submitted to us from lots of talented authors, and Ben's was the one that stood out head and shoulders above the rest. It’s a really interesting concept," says Weir. "It's not just trope sci-fi with an evil empire of bad guys and some plucky rebels. Ben came up with a unique story with a unique angle. Audio is quickly becoming a larger and larger medium. Everyone's on the go, and now for the first time in history we all have computers in our pocket capable of storing multiple audiobooks to last us years. It's a great time to revive the old art of radio plays, and I think this is a great way to do it.” Weir's enthusiasm for the project is clear, and we can't wait to check it out. And we won't have to, because it releases today! " Exoplanet " is available starting Nov. 5 exclusively from Audible for members of its subscription tiers or as an a la carte option. One crew. One planet. Three timelines. No one survives alone. A sci-fi thriller executive produced by Andy Weir (#1 bestselling author of Project Hail Mary , The Martian ), with an all-star cast led by Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose and John Leguizamo. Exoplanet is free for Audible members, but also available for purchase separately. View Deal

item.title: Sony revives the original Walkman headphones, adds USB-C
item.description: Color us nostalgic. Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player. In this marketing image Sony shared, you can see the Walkman TPS-L2. Credit: Sony Originally called the "MDR-3L2," the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. The lightweight, on-ear headphones are a contrast to the bulky headsets that are popular these days, which use wide, cushioned headbands for long-term comfort and large earcups that can support big drivers and are often heavily padded for noise isolation. item.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
item.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. The post 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
item.description: Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools . Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn't want to use AI. Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing. The gist of the new policy, according to Google's blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts. When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times , which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it's probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google's educational AI system will operate. Google's approach may not be entirely altruistic, but it technically offers schools more choice and control than they have now. Instead of Google turning off search, it will let schools make that decision based on their internal AI policies. Read full article Comments

item.title: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
item.description: ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide. At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said. Read full article Comments

item.title: ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor
item.description: A former Governor of Edo State and National Legal Adviser of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Oserheimen Osunbor, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being jittery ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Osunbor said the APC did not want a strong candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “I have said that repeatedly, they (APC) are afraid of any strong candidate running against President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election,” Osunbor said. ﻿ The ADC legal adviser said the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, were continuing with their campaigns because they believed the court judgment nullifying Atiku’s candidacy would not stand. “Our presidential candidate (Atiku Abubakar) and the presidential campaign is going on, unperturbed because we believe that this judgment will not stand and cannot stand,” he said. Osunbor said the party would appeal the judgment to ensure that a higher court sets it aside. He expressed optimism that Atiku would survive the current challenge, insisting that the former Vice President had the support of the people. “Atiku will survive because the people are behind him. The force of the people will be greater than the force of those who want to enslave Nigerians,” he said. Osunbor’s comments followed Thursday’s judgment by the Federal High Court in Abuja, which sacked the David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated actions taken by the party under the leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the ADC. The party has rejected the ruling and vowed to challenge it at the appellate court. The post ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor appeared first on Channels Television .
